articles.title: Firefox 161 updates that can help save time over the holidays
articles.summary:
Lighten the holiday load with these four Firefox 161 updates
The holiday season, the festive season, the “how is the year almost over?” season. Whatever you call it, there’s a lot to get done. Gifts to buy, meals to plan, travel details to sort out, all while your regular responsibilities refuse to take time off.
In Firefox 161, we’re introducing a few new updates that can help you save time during the busiest months of the year, plus a new place to browse when you have a few minutes to cross something off your list. So you can cut down on the time spent prepping for the holidays, and get back to the people you’re doing it all for.
Set VPN rules for individual sites
Searching for the perfect gift? You might want to use a VPN to compare how prices differ by region. Sites like your bank or favorite streaming service, however, might work better without it.
Firefox’s free built-in VPN on desktop now lets you choose which sites automatically open with VPN on, and which open with it off. This way, your preferences are applied automatically, and you can save time skipping the constant toggling on/off every time you visit a different site.
Open the VPN panel from your toolbar and select Manage VPN rules, or go to Settings → Privacy & Security → VPN → Manage VPN rules. Add a website and choose Always on or Always off. Once a rule is set, that site will automatically open with your VPN preferences on future visits.

Tan solo unos pocos meses después del final de su temporada 4, Apple ha renovado oficialmente Ted Lasso para una temporada 5. articles.title: 1.5 Million Impacted by Data Breach at South Korean Electric Company KEPCO
articles.summary:
South Korean state-owned electric company Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO, KRX: 015760, NYSE: KEP) has disclosed a data breach impacting approximately 1.5 million people.
The incident, the company says, involved KEPCO ON, its integrated customer service portal, and the supplier relationship management (SRM) platform, which handles procurement and service contracts.
KEPCO attributed the incident to an external attacker and noted the growing sophistication of AI-driven cyberattacks. It did not disclose how the attacker gained access or confirm that AI was used in this breach.
According to KEPCO, it suspended the affected services immediately after discovering the incident, blocked external access, conducted a thorough review of the relevant systems, and took remediation actions.
On November 20, the company confirmed that data was exfiltrated from its systems, including electricity customer and SRM user information.
From KEPCO ON, the hackers stole the personal information of 650,487 people, including names, addresses, phone numbers, unique ID numbers, customer numbers, card numbers and details, bank names, bank account numbers, account-holder names, card issuers, cardholder names, and billing/payment details.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
  November 4, 2026
- Source:
  Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
  Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

articles.title: Ladybird, un navegador creado desde cero sin usar el motor de Chrome, ya se puede probar
articles.summary:
Ladybird, un navegador de internet con un motor propio, escrito desde cero y no basado en el de Chrome, Safari ni Firefox, está disponible desde el 23 de noviembre en versión alfa para Mac y Linux. Su fundador, Andreas Kling, lo anunció en el sitio del proyecto. Una versión alfa es una primera etapa pública de pruebas.
Kling advirtió que algunas páginas no funcionarán y que el programa fallará a veces. También señaló que no hace promesas sobre la seguridad y pidió a los especialistas que intenten vulnerarlo e informen cómo.
El proyecto pide a los usuarios que reporten desde el propio navegador los sitios que se vean mal. Tras un cierre inesperado, el usuario puede leer el informe del error y decidir si lo envía. Los detalles figuran en la política de privacidad del proyecto.
Qué es un motor de navegador y por qué importa
El motor es la parte del navegador que lee el código de una página web y la convierte en lo que se ve en pantalla. El sitio de Ladybird sostiene que solo un puñado de motores sustentan toda la web y que cada uno depende de una empresa con intereses propios.
Este navegador se define como independiente: según su sitio, no es una bifurcación de Chromium, Gecko ni WebKit, los motores que usan Chrome y Edge, Firefox y Safari respectivamente, y no utiliza código de Blink, WebKit ni Gecko.

articles.title: GTA 6 : Rockstar a caché un très gros secret qui vient d’être découvert par les joueurs
articles.summary:
Un portail caché dans GTA 6 qui permet de replonger dans le Vice City de 2002. Et, au bout de la quête, Jason, l’un des deux héros du jeu, repart avec la chemise hawaïenne de Tommy Vercetti et sa moto.
Pour les puristes prêts à retourner chaque mètre carré de Leonida, le studio a dissimulé un véritable voyage dans le temps, pensé comme un hommage à GTA Vice City.
Un portail secret caché derrière un code de triche de 2002 sur GTA 6
On doit la découverte au youtubeur australien Memeio, qui vient de mettre en lumière un easter egg de GTA 6 de grande ampleur La quête cachée commence dans la tour radio Badger R&D, à Key Lento, où un interrupteur affiche le logo du Malibu Club sur une télévision. Il faut ensuite activer, dans l’ordre, douze sous-stations électriques réparties sur la carte, sans voyage rapide ni changement de personnage. Les lettres peintes sur leurs murs forment « LIFEISPASSINGMEBY », le code de triche de GTA Vice City qui accélérait l’horloge du jeu. Un SMS envoie alors le joueur au réacteur 2 de la centrale de Turtle Head, à visiter entre 19 h et 6 h. Oui, le voyage dans le temps se mérite.
Un portail violet y apparaît. En le traversant, Jason quitte les graphismes réalistes de GTA 6 pour les personnages anguleux et les textures d’époque de la PlayStation 2. Il se retrouve dans le célèbre Malibu Club, recréé tel qu’il apparaissait il y a vingt-quatre ans. La nostalgie est là.

Tanto que en 2017 se estrenó una secuela, Blade Runner 2049, dirigida por Denis Villeneuve. Ahora, es turno de una tercera entrega, esta vez en forma de serie. articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
  November 7, 2026
- Source:
  University of Regensburg
- Summary:
  Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert…

articles.title: Jensen Huang reveló a la junta directiva de Nvidia más relaciones extramatrimoniales antes de su regreso
articles.summary:
Jensen Huang, cofundador y director ejecutivo de Nvidia, confirmó ante la junta directiva de la compañía nuevas relaciones extramatrimoniales durante una reunión, según reveló The Wall Street Journal. El encuentro se produjo horas antes de que los directores votaran por unanimidad su reincorporación al cargo, apenas 11 días después de haber renunciado.
El propio Huang ya había admitido semanas atrás una infidelidad vinculada a Alice Huang, una ejecutiva señalada por autoridades estadounidenses por presuntos nexos con inteligencia china. Pero la reunión del domingo sumó un capítulo que, según las fuentes citadas por el diario, va más allá de los dos vínculos que ya habían trascendido públicamente.
Qué reveló Huang ante la junta directiva
Durante el encuentro, los directores interrogaron a Huang durante varias horas sobre su conducta, su transparencia y su franqueza respecto a los episodios. Según el reporte, el ejecutivo mostró arrepentimiento por su comportamiento y reconoció “aventuras adicionales más allá de las dos que habían sido ampliamente reportadas”.
El texto no precisa el número exacto de relaciones adicionales ni la identidad de las personas involucradas, aunque otras coberturas periodísticas sugieren que la cifra total de vínculos alegados podría llegar a por lo menos cuatro.
Pese a la decisión de reincorporarlo, la junta concluyó que Huang había violado el código de conducta de la empresa, tanto por sostener esas relaciones como por no haberlas revelado a tiempo. …

articles.title: NVIDIA reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO; Sarvam unveils upgraded model amid Token Factory row
articles.summary:
NVIDIA reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO; Sarvam unveils upgraded model amid Token Factory row
Nvidia has reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as its president, CEO, and board director, less than two weeks after his resignation from the company. In other news, Sarvam’s new AI model promises better performance at a lower cost.
Dear Reader,
In a quick turn of events, Nvidia has reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as its president, CEO, and board director.
This development comes less than two weeks after Huang’s resignation from the company. It follows discussions between Huang and the board, alongside inputs from senior US government officials, the company said.
In other news, Zoho’s Sridhar Vembu has said AI is transforming coding and intellectual work the way mechanisation impacted farming and weaving.

articles.title: OpenAI, Cisco Unveil Open Source Tool to Shield Unpatched Linux Systems

OpenAI and Cisco on Monday unveiled Shirudo, an open source security platform that uses AI agents to prevent the exploitation of vulnerabilities in Linux systems and applications.
The project is an AI-focused rewrite of Cisco-owned Isovalent’s Tetragon runtime security platform. Tetragon was open-sourced in 2022, and it also powers Cisco’s Live Protect vulnerability mitigation technology.
Shirudo is designed to help defenders address the challenges introduced by AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery and exploitation, which is increasing pressure on organizations to deploy patches quickly.
The tool leverages eBPF technology to modify Linux kernel behavior without restarting the OS.
According to Cisco and OpenAI, agents can analyze vulnerability information, generate so-called ‘shields’ to prevent exploitation, and test their effectiveness without disrupting important services. Security teams still retain control over which shields are deployed.
Protections are digitally signed and verified before deployment, with mechanisms designed to prevent even attackers with root privileges from disabling kernel-level enforcement.
In a controlled test targeting the recent Java4Shell vulnerability, a shield generated using OpenAI’s Codex blocked an exploitation attempt targeting an Elasticsearch instance without requiring a restart.

articles.title: A Link Is Not Architecture: Why Multi-Die Systems Need More Than Die-to-Die Connectivity
articles.summary:
Maintaining consistent communication behavior, integration, and security across configurations.
The system-on-chip (SoC) transformed semiconductor design by bringing the major functions of an electronic system onto one die, an integration that shaped chip architecture for years. Multi-die design is now changing the model again, distributing system functionality across multiple dies within a single package.
While this approach gives engineers greater flexibility to align semiconductor design with system requirements, bringing these designs to life takes more than a die-to-die link to transport transactions across the package. It requires a system architecture that manages how data moves between dies.
In AI and high-performance computing (HPC) systems, multi-die architectures enable teams to scale compute and select an appropriate process technology for each part of the design. These partitioning choices determine which transactions remain within a die and which must cross die boundaries. Treating each boundary independently increases integration and verification effort, complicates performance management, and reduces the practical value of chiplet reuse.
Still, managing communication across these die boundaries requires a clear separation between the physical interface that transports transactions and the system architecture that manages them. ¿Qué pasa en una casa inteligente cuando se cae internet?
Una avería en la fibra no tiene por qué dejar fuera de juego toda la domótica, pero sí puede impedir controlar luces, cámaras o electrodomésticos
Televisores, altavoces inteligentes, termostatos, cámaras de vigilancia, electrodomésticos… Cada vez utilizamos más dispositivos conectados y pocas veces nos paramos a pensar qué pasaría en caso de producirse un fallo con la conexión a internet. ¿Seguirían funcionando como si nada? ¿Podríamos controlarlos de alguna manera? Lo cierto es que no hay una respuesta universal, y al final todo depende del producto concreto y del tipo de conexión que se use para configurarlos en la red doméstica.
Lo primero que hay que tener en cuenta es que, aunque a menudo hablamos de internet (o la conexión) y del Wi-Fi como sinónimos, la realidad es que no son lo mismo: internet es la red global que permite acceder a páginas web, plataformas y servidores externos, mientras Wi-Fi es la tecnología que conecta nuestros dispositivos con la red local del hogar sin cables. ¿Por qué es importante esta diferencia? Australia has lost one of its most distinguished ecologists and conservation champions, Emeritus Professor Chris Dickman.
Chris’s achievements and legacy are vast, much like his beloved Simpson Desert that he and his research team – known as “the ratcatchers” – have studied for well over 30 years. He and his team would camp out under the stars, carefully trapping and monitoring the desert’s animals and plants.
Without Chris, we wouldn’t know just how important even small but ferocious predators are in structuring ecological communities. One example is the brush-tailed mulgara, which preys on and regulates numbers of other predators, including the lesser hairy-footed dunnart.
Chris touched many in both his personal and professional roles. The authors of this article each knew Chris for many years.
Chris was honoured in a celebratory forum and festschrift, a collection of written tributes, in June that was attended by about 200 people and another 140 online. He died on November 17, 2026.
Science and service
Chris’s impressive career was marked by a dedication to the scientific field and service to the wider community.
He was an internationally renowned leader in wildlife conservation who studied everything from the small marsupial Antechinus to dunnarts, long-haired rats, mulgaras, quolls, sandy inland and spinifex hopping mice and the Tasmanian devil, to name but a few species.

Warrantless wiretapping proponents are rushing to beat the looming blue wave.

According to Anthropic, existing Claude protections can identify potentially harmful requests made individually, but EFS adds a monitoring layer that can detect suspicious patterns across multiple requests that may appear benign when analyzed individually.
The system targets organizations that use Claude under zero data retention agreements and have so far relied only on classifiers that analyze each request in isolation.
EFS is designed to detect both deliberate misuse of AI, such as AI-powered cyberattacks, and incidents where AI agents go beyond what their operator intended, such as the cases where agents exploited vulnerabilities to gain access to real-world systems.
With EFS, organizations store conversation data in their own cloud and protect it with their own encryption keys and access policies.

En cuestión de laboratorios de IA, hay actualmente dos estilos principales: los que acostumbran a liberar los pesos y aquellos que prefieren mantenerlos cerrados y cobrar por usarlos. La tendencia había colocado a los laboratorios chinos del lado abierto y a los estadounidenses en la acera contraria, aunque poco a poco las líneas se juntan. Z.ai es la prueba.
Nuevo modelo insignia: GLM-5.4. Si el anterior ya era bueno en tareas como la programación, la empresa ajusta esas capacidades con un cambio de arquitectura que apunta a la eficiencia. Según Z.ai, GLM-5.4 es su primer modelo insignia con arquitectura Loop Transformer.
Según la empresa, GLM-5.4 rinde como modelos de entre 2 y 3 billones de parámetros, aunque de momento no ha presentado los benchmarks. Ofrece hasta 200 tokens por segundo fuera de las horas punta (entre 70 y 80 cuando hay más carga), admite hasta un millón de tokens de contexto, incluye modo de razonamiento y suma visión a su especialidad, la programación.
Como pegas, la propia Z.ai reconoce que el nuevo modelo tiende a enredarse en razonamientos demasiado largos. Y las primeras pruebas independientes apuntan hacia esa misma dirección: en KingBench 4 tardó 431 minutos frente a los 109 de Gemini 4 Neon. GLM-5.4 gastó unas 15 veces más tokens.
No hay pesos abiertos ni fecha para ellos. El anuncio del nuevo modelo nos deja por escrito las capacidades y la posibilidad de probarlo en las suscripciones que Z.ai ofrece a los usuarios: actualmente está en todos los…

articles.title: Une arnaque vise les stations-service et les distributeurs de billets en France : comment éviter de se faire piéger ?
articles.summary:
Nous avons ici affaire à une arnaque sophistiquée qui cible plus particulièrement les stations-service et les distributeurs de billets. Plusieurs victimes ont été recensées en France ces derniers jours, avec des montants dérobés allant de 500 à plus de 1 000 euros. Il faut dire que cette arnaque est difficilement repérable. Une victime peut effectuer un paiement ou retirer de l’argent en saisissant son code PIN, sans rien remarquer. Cependant, un point précis peut alerter sur la situation.
Une minuscule caméra et un lecteur de carte piégé pour vider vos comptes bancaires
Une nouvelle arnaque, particulièrement élaborée, a été repérée à plusieurs reprises ces derniers jours en France. Cette arnaque vise plus particulièrement les stations-service et les distributeurs de billets. En d’autres termes, tous les dispositifs qui demandent d’insérer une carte bancaire et de saisir un code PIN. Le mode de fonctionnement de cette arnaque est, il faut le dire, sophistiqué. Comme l’explique BFMTV, les arnaqueurs parviennent à intégrer un dispositif dans le lecteur de carte d’un système de paiement. Ce dispositif est ensuite capable d’intercepter les données échangées avec la puce de la carte bancaire. Il est ici plus précisément question de skimming, une technique qui consiste à insérer un boîtier très fin dans le lecteur afin de récupérer les données de la carte.
En parallèle, les arnaqueurs placent une minuscule caméra juste au-dessus du pavé numérique destiné à saisir le code bancaire. …

Une voiture électrique lancée en 1996 par GM

La voiture ne roulait plus avec un pare-brise cassé, de l'eau infiltrée et, plus insolite, des ratons laveurs qui avaient élu domicile à l'emplacement de la batterie. General Motors n'a jamais vendu l'EV1 aux particuliers

articles.title: New Shirudo tool uses AI to shield unpatched Linux systems from exploits
articles.summary:
OpenAI and Cisco launched an open-source Linux security tool named Shirudo that deploys temporary runtime protections to block vulnerability exploitation while administrators prepare and roll out patches, without restarting services.
Shirudo leverages the eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter) mechanism in Linux to monitor for suspicious activity and deploy targeted protections called "shields."
eBPF is a Linux technology that lets programs run in a controlled environment within the operating system's kernel without modifying its source code or requiring a restart.
It enables real-time monitoring of system and network activity, performance analysis, and enforcement of targeted security protections, making it an ideal operational basis for Shirudo.
Shirudo’s shields aim to block malicious behavior in a targeted way, leaving legitimate application operations undisturbed. OpenAI highlights four core capabilities for the tool:
- Live protection: Blocks vulnerable code paths without restarting systems, letting operators assess shield impact before enforcing them.
- AI-assisted defense: Enables agents to investigate vulnerabilities, develop shields, and validate their effectiveness, with deployment remaining under human control.
- Trusted deployment: Uses cryptographic signatures, Linux's eBPF verifier, and kernel security controls to prevent unauthorized modifications.
- Hardware-backed verification: Uses Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs) to provide verifiable records of shields bei…

articles.title: Activision estudia usar los chats de voz de Discord para entrenar a los NPC de Call of Duty
articles.summary:
Activision presentó una solicitud de patente para un sistema que podría aprender de las conversaciones de voz de los jugadores y asociarlas con acontecimientos de un videojuego. La propuesta contempla aplicaciones externas como Discord y TeamSpeak como posibles fuentes de audio. Luego, un modelo de aprendizaje automático podría generar respuestas para personajes controlados por la computadora, conocidos como NPC.
El documento, titulado Methods and Systems for Applying Machine Learning to Generate Gameplay Audio, fue presentado el 16 de julio de 2026 y publicado por la Oficina de Patentes y Marcas de Estados Unidos el 12 de noviembre. Una aplicación de esta idea podría verse en un juego como Call of Duty: por ejemplo, un NPC podría festejar una eliminación o burlarse del jugador después de una derrota con una frase inspirada en las conversaciones que suelen darse durante las partidas.
Cómo aprenderían los NPC de las conversaciones
El sistema identificaría eventos que el juego puede reconocer, como una eliminación, la muerte del jugador, una victoria o el final de una ronda. Luego, buscaría fragmentos de audio cercanos a esos momentos para asociar una reacción con lo ocurrido.
La descripción ofrece como ejemplo analizar los diez segundos anteriores y posteriores a un evento. Así, si un compañero celebra una baja o se burla después de que alguien pierda, el modelo podría relacionar esas palabras y su tono con el momento correspondiente. articles.summary:
Shortening the path from design intent to verified implementation could put custom silicon within reach of more teams.
The age of physical AI is here, and with it comes a significant increase in the demand of custom silicon.
By 2025, five million industrial robots were operating worldwide. As these systems become more capable, their demands on silicon become more distinct. Each must balance computation and memory with the realities of power, latency, reliability, and security.
Fig. 1: Annual installations of industrial robots, 5 largest markets, 2025. Source: International Federation of Robotics, World Robotics 2026. Chart redrawn by ChipAgents.
For humanoid robots in particular, application-specific hardware can provide the agility and speed required to perform specialized tasks in real time. As those requirements diverge, specialized ASICs become more attractive, because they can be optimized for the exact workloads, latency targets, power envelopes, and operating environments of a particular system.
The constraint to this innovation is development speed: AI models and software evolve faster than the conventional silicon tape out cycles, creating a need to accelerate the entire path from design intent and exploration to physical implementation and validation.

articles.title: Via Láctea é mais pesada do que se imaginava
articles.summary:
A Via Láctea é ainda mais massiva do que algumas estimativas anteriores sugeriam. Uma nova análise realizada por astrônomos da colaboração Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) calculou que nossa galáxia possui aproximadamente 1,19 trilhão de vezes a massa do Sol. O resultado representa a estimativa mais precisa já produzida sobre a massa total da nossa galáxia.
O cálculo considera tanto a matéria comum quanto a matéria escura, componente invisível que exerce influência gravitacional sobre estrelas e outros objetos cósmicos.
A dificuldade de determinar esse número está justamente no fato de que não conseguimos observar toda a massa da Via Láctea diretamente. Estimativas anteriores variavam bastante, indo de 500 bilhões a três trilhões de massas solares.
O novo trabalho, ainda disponível como preprint e sem revisão por pares, combina grande quantidade de dados astronômicos com diferentes métodos de cálculo para reduzir essa incerteza.
Como os cientistas calcularam a massa da Via Láctea?
- Para estimar a massa da galáxia, os pesquisadores analisaram 10.036 estrelas dos tipos RR Lyrae e estrelas do ramo horizontal azul, identificadas nos dados da segunda publicação do DESI (Data Release 2);
- Essas estrelas têm característica importante para o estudo: apresentam luminosidade relativamente previsível. Isso permite que os astrônomos estimem suas distâncias com maior precisão;

articles.summary:
Pieter van der Does, co-founder and Co-CEO of Dutch Fintech Adyen, is stepping down from his executive role after 20 years at the helm of one of Europe’s most prominent technology companies.
In an announcement on 23 November 2026, marking Adyen’s 20th anniversary, the company said van der Does will retire on 31 December 2026, and Ingo Uytdehaage, Co-CEO since 2023, will become sole CEO
“After 20 years, this is the right moment for me to step down on a positive note and with a very good feeling. Adyen has been my life’s work, and I’m incredibly proud of what our teams and customers have built together over the past two decades. Ingo and I have worked very closely together as Co-CEOs, and now we have completed the transition,” said van der Does, co-founder and co-CEO of Adyen.
Arnout Schuijff and van der Does launched Adyen in 2006, and the company was formally incorporated on 23 November 2006, when Schuijff visited a notary in Amsterdam to formally establish the company. Van der Does, who was on a sabbatical in Brazil at the time, followed the proceedings remotely over Skype.
Before starting Adyen, the co-founders had previously worked together at payments company Bibit, and their shared ambition became Adyen, which means “doing it again” in Surinamese. In his farewell letter, Van der Does says, “Adyen outgrew our wildest imagination.”

articles.title: Austrália ameaça Google e Meta com multas de até 5% da receita global
Amazon says hackers’ AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
articles.summary:
Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server.
The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers. The agents then exploited the vulnerability and gained full control of the system.
“These findings show that agentic offensive operations are already happening, and defenders should prepare for the speed and persistence these tools enable,” Amazon said.
Made for defenders, but attackers like it too
Cairn is an open source AI problem-solving engine whose first validated domain is autonomous penetration testing. Users give it a task or goal and, optionally, hints for achieving it. A server maintains a shared graph containing facts and hints. A dispatcher reads the graph, schedules tasks, manages containers, and writes the protocol. The dispatcher can then assign each project to a dedicated worker container, each of which runs multiple agents concurrently. Cairn is model-agnostic and can be used on worker back ends, including Claude Code, Codex, and Pi. Researchers from security firm Palo Alto Ne…

articles.title: ‘Bye AI music’: Tidal announces full ban on AI-generated songs — as Deezer reveals 57% of people have AI tunes lurking in their playlists
articles.summary:
Tidal says it’s ‘banning’ AI music from December — streaming giant will delete 27 million songs from its library and reject 80,000 AI-generated tracks a day
Making music human again
- Tidal says it's banning all 100% AI-generated music from its service
- The policy will start from December 9 and lead to 29 million track deletions
- Meanwhile, Deezer research has discovered most music streaming users unknowingly have AI music in their playlists
As Spotify gears up to launch its AI-powered remix and covers feature in 2027, Tidal is moving in the opposite direction — announcing today that it’s banning all AI-generated tracks from its platform, starting on December 9.
The news, announced on X, follows its decision back in July to demonetize and label 100% AI-generated recordings. This time, it’s getting rid of them completely. This will result in roughly 29 million songs being deleted, and an estimated 80,000-85,000 rejected songs per day.
It's also a move that makes sense for Tidal, with the streaming service revealing that roughly 6% of its catalog is currently AI-generated, and that roughly 43% of all tracks added over the last 90 days have been AI.
However, there’s clearly not much appetite for those tracks, because 96% of all AI-badged tracks got zero streams in the last 90 days.
Unpopular yet hard to avoid

articles.title: Frankfurt-based CommerzVentures closes €50 million Fund IV, betting on early-stage FinTech and AI
articles.summary:
CommerzVentures, a Frankfurt-based specialist venture capital firm focused on financial services, has closed its fourth fund at €50 million.
The fourth fund — CommerzVentures IV (Fund IV) — is anchored by Commerzbank and is deliberately smaller than its predecessors; the firm managed over €550 million across three prior funds, including €300 million in Fund III.
“Fund IV is deliberately smaller because we want to invest earlier. We aim to combine early conviction with the experience, industry connections and hands-on support founders need to build their businesses,” said Judith Vogel, Partner, CommerzVentures.

The CommerzVentures IV is jointly led by general partners Heiko Schwender and Vogel, supported by venture partners and senior advisers. GreyNoise believes the threat actor has been using agentic harnesses and systems to weaponize vulnerabilities, find vulnerable assets, and automatically exploit them. The automated operations were complemented by hands-on-keyboard activity.

articles.title: Huang reportedly admitted to more than two affairs to Nvidia's board
articles.summary:
In a complete U-turn, Nvidia’s board on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as the CEO and president of the chipmaker, just a fortnight after he resigned.
During a meeting before his reinstatement, however, Huang admitted to more affairs beyond the two that have been reported in the news, according to The Wall Street Journal.
Early in November, Huang admitted to an extramarital affair in a letter to employees. At the time, he was ostensibly talking about his relationship with Megaspeed executive and alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (not related to Jensen). Later, it was reported that he’d also had a relationship with Nvidia’s VP of health, Kimberly Powell.
Afterwards, Reuters reported that he also had an affair with another employee.
It’s not clear which affairs Huang admitted to during this recent conversation with Nvidia’s board of directors.
Huang’s return was spurred by a personal intervention from the U.S. government, Nvidia’s board said in a statement on Monday, and President Donald Trump apparently called the board to bat for Huang’s reinstatement.
The Wall Street Journal reports that over the weekend, U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche told Trump and Vice President JD Vance that the Justice Department wasn’t investigating Huang and there was no evidence that he was a national security risk, after which both contacted the company’s board.
Huang received a “hero’s welcome” at Nvidia’s HQ, with several employees applauding his return.

McDonald's Japan, the fast-food giant's Japanese subsidiary, has disclosed a data breach after attackers accessed a database containing sensitive information for users of the company's official smartphone app.
Founded in 1940, McDonald's is now a multinational fast-food chain that operates more than 40,000 restaurants in more than 100 countries and serves tens of millions of customers daily.
In a Friday statement, the company's Japanese subsidiary confirmed that threat actors gained access to its official app's database and said the exposed information includes the users' product purchase history, IP addresses, mobile device location data, and customer management IDs (which cannot be used to identify the customers' email addresses or member IDs).
McDonald's Japan also added that the exposed data doesn't include the affected customers' names, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses, or credit card information.
While it has yet to reveal when it detected the attack or how many individuals had their data stolen, the company said a follow-up investigation found no service disruption or misuse of official apps as a result of the incident.
"We are working to invalidate any credentials used for unauthorized access, investigate the relevant systems, and report to the Personal Information Protection Commission," it said. "In addition, we will strive to strengthen security measures and prevent recurrence."

Designing the microarchitecture involved balancing software-visible architectural behavior, RTL implementation details, and internal performance and power tradeoffs, which together introduced verification requirements that extended well beyond isolated hardware blocks. Homo erectus was walking around mainland Asia at least 60,000 years more recently than archaeologists thought. A handful of teeth from two caves in southern China’s Guangxi Province just filled in a significant gap in the fossil record of a region that’s vital to the story of how our genus, Homo, took over the world.
The chemical makeup of the teeth’s enamel suggests that, over the course of their lives, these Homo erectus moved across surprisingly large distances and made their living in dense tropical rainforests—an environment we’d previously assumed that only our species had ever gained a real foothold in. Baxian and Naxian are a pair of limestone caves that lie 15 kilometers apart along a karst valley corridor in southern China. University of Copenhagen paleoanthropologist Frido Welker and his colleagues unearthed a total of nine hominin teeth from among the more than 18,000 bones and fragments from non-hominin animals found there. articles.title: Prepare Market Data for Forecasting with NVIDIA Megatron Core
articles.summary:
Market data arrives as a stream of trades and quotes: every execution, bid, and ask, timestamped to the microsecond. Preparing this data for AI-based market forecasting requires turning price and volume histories into consistent inputs for model training and inference. A common first step is aggregating the data into bars—one row per instrument per time unit—with price, volume, and other statistics. Neural networks can learn patterns from these histories across instruments and forecast horizons.
NVIDIA Megatron Core is an open-source library of GPU-optimized components for training transformer models at scale. Megatron-LM is a GitHub repository that combines that library with preconfigured training scripts. A preprocessing script turns intraday market bars into model-ready tensors, and a dataset provider feeds them into Megatron’s distributed training loop.
This post shows how to preprocess market-bar data and train a model with Megatron-LM to forecast returns and trading volume across multiple horizons.
Forecast returns and trading volume
Price and volume remain continuous features. A learned patch embedding turns each group of observations into a model input without converting market values into text.

articles.summary:
Written by: George Manuelian, Chief Strategy Officer, RapidFort
The modern software stack has become an iceberg. The application code customers and security teams see at the surface is only a small portion of what is being shipped. Beneath it sit operating systems, frameworks, libraries, packages, and transitive dependencies, with much of it drawn from open source or third parties.
As AI accelerates software development, that hidden complexity has become an even more critical security challenge.
For business and technology leaders, the question is no longer simply how many vulnerabilities exist. It is where does meaningful risk live, which vulnerabilities can be exploited in our environment, and how we can reduce that risk without turning developers into full-time vulnerability managers.
The answer requires a fundamental shift from vulnerability accumulation to continuous software resilience.
First step: Recognizing composition of modern software
The typical containerized stack is layers of base operating system software, packages, libraries, language frameworks and dependencies, and the application itself. The application a company writes may represent only a small portion of what it ultimately ships.
That is important because vulnerabilities multiply. A vulnerable package in a base image is not necessarily one vulnerability in practice; it can be replicated across every application and container that uses that image.

articles.title: Why Photonic Design Is Becoming a System-Level Challenge
articles.summary:
A component can meet its individual design targets and still behave differently as part of a complete optical link.
Photonic engineers make design decisions at many levels.
A laser has its own performance requirements. So does an optical fiber. The interface between them introduces another set of variables. Ultimately, those individual components have to perform together as part of a complete optical link.
If the individual pieces meet their design targets, will the complete system perform as expected?
Not necessarily.
A Keysight EDA-Photonics Design (VPIphotonics) study of short-reach datacenter links provides a useful example. Two multimode VCSEL channels were designed with comparable signal characteristics and evaluated with a wideband multimode fiber. Yet when evaluated as complete transmission links, the two channels produced different results.
Understanding the difference in performance requires looking beyond any single component.
The VPIphotonics study modeled 26.5625 GBaud PAM4 transmission over 150 meters of wideband multimode fiber, using VCSEL channels operating at 850 nm and 910 nm. Each VCSEL was modeled with four transverse modes, and the link considered coupling conditions and receiver models.
25 Gbaud PAM4 with a multimode VCSEL and OM4 fiber.
At first glance, the two channels seemed comparable.
The calculated 3 dB bandwidth was 27.0 GHz at 850 nm and 27.8 GHz at 910 nm.
But that wasn’t the end of the story.

A jury has found Huawei guilty of stealing US trade secrets, as reported earlier by NBC News and Bloomberg. The verdict, handed down in a federal court in New York, concludes a years-long legal battle that accused the Chinese telecom giant of stealing source code and proprietary technology from several companies, including T-Mobile, Cisco, and Motorola.
Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
The Chinese telecom giant was also found guilty of bank fraud.
The Department of Justice’s 2018 criminal indictment against Huawei came to light following the arrest of the company’s CFO, Wanzhou Meng, whom the agency accused of fraud. Though the indictment against Meng was eventually dismissed, she admitted to misleading banks over Huawei’s operations in Iran as part of a deferred prosecution agreement. The US government blacklisted Huawei in 2019 over national security concerns.
In total, the jury found Huawei guilty of 10 of 12 criminal counts, including money laundering, violating US sanctions, bank fraud, wire fraud, and conspiracy to defraud the US. The government, including NASA, has been operating on a “continuing resolution” since that time. articles.title: Contrata como empleada de hogar durante 4 meses a la mujer de un amigo y consigue que tenga derecho a paro en Vigo

Un juez de Santiago de Compostela ha anulado la multa de 7.501 euros que la Inspección de Trabajo impuso a un empresario de Vigo por contratar durante cuatro meses como empleada del hogar a la mujer de un amigo, una oficinista de más de 52 años que, gracias a esas cotizaciones, acabó cobrando el subsidio por desempleo. Tal y como ha contado La Voz de Galicia, la sentencia, dictada el 22 de septiembre de 2026, concluye que aquel contrato fue real.
Un contrato justo después de la negativa. La mujer había pedido en Vigo el subsidio para mayores de 52 años, pero se lo denegaron a mediados de noviembre de 2022. Y apenas dos semanas más tarde, el 1 de diciembre, el amigo de la familia la contrató a tiempo parcial como su empleada del hogar, en una relación laboral que terminó a finales de marzo de 2023. Poco después, ya en el paro, volvió a solicitar el subsidio, y esta vez se lo concedieron al acreditar esos cuatro meses cotizados.
Lo que vio la Inspección. Para los inspectores, aquello olía a fraude de ley. Y es que el empresario nunca había necesitado una empleada del hogar ni contrató a otra después de prescindir de esta, que además era la esposa de un amigo con el que había coincidido en el trabajo. "The operation targeted a criminal market worth billions of euros annually, in which illegal streaming providers sell unauthorised access to premium television channels, live sports and films, often collecting subscription payments through cryptocurrency."

articles.title: Why the US Army is about to blow up nearly 10,000 pounds of unstable explosives in Iowa
articles.summary:
The US Army is moving ahead with plans to detonate the nation’s stockpile of lead azide at an ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa, at approximately 9:00AM CST on Wednesday. The Verge reached out to experts on what to expect, and will keep this post updated.
Why the US Army is about to blow up nearly 10,000 pounds of unstable explosives in Iowa
The US Army is scrambling to contain any potential lead pollution that could spread if an old stockpile of explosives blows up.
What material is the Army planning to detonate?
There are 68 drums holding about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, an unstable chemical compound created to detonate munitions like grenades. The US started using lead azide as a primary explosive almost a century ago before “moving away” from it about 15 years ago because of how difficult the material is to store and transport, Robert Cekada, director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), said in a Tuesday press briefing. At that point, the US transferred its remaining stockpile of lead azide to the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. Lead azide will explode at 350 degrees Celsius (662F). But it is also sensitive to flame, friction, or sudden shock, including fluctuations in temperature.

articles.title: Mozilla explica por que não há um Firefox "puro" para iPhone
articles.summary:
Mozilla explica por que não há um Firefox “puro” para iPhone
Mozilla afirma que regras impostas pela Apple são complexas e inviabilizam o Firefox de ter seu próprio motor no iOS.
A Mozilla lançou a primeira versão do Firefox para iPhone em 2015. Mas, até hoje, o navegador não conta com uma implementação totalmente “pura” no iOS, com motor próprio. Em tom de desabafo, a organização explicou o motivo. Saiba desde já que, sim, a Mozilla culpa a Apple por isso.
Quando falamos de motor, nos referimos ao componente central do navegador, que interpreta o código de páginas web escrito em padrões como HTML, CSS e JavaScript, e transforma esse conjunto de informações em um conteúdo visual e interativo para o usuário.
Hoje, a maior parte dos navegadores é baseada no projeto Chromium, a exemplo do Microsoft Edge, do Opera, do Brave e, claro, do Google Chrome. No Chromium, o motor utilizado é o Blink.
O Firefox é diferente, pois conta com um motor próprio: o Gecko. Mas, no iOS, o navegador é executado a partir do WebKit, motor mantido pela Apple que, como tal, é a base do Safari.
É aqui que está o ponto de conflito: se dependesse da Mozilla, o Firefox também contaria com o Gecko no iPhone.
A Apple exigia que os navegadores para iOS usassem o WebKit sob o argumento de que essa condição favorecia aspectos como segurança, privacidade e desempenho. Isso mudou em 2024, quando a Digital Markets Act (DMA) passou a vigorar. Trata-se de uma legislação da União Europeia que busca aumentar a concorr…

The ESX updates resolve seven security issues as well, including three critical-severity weaknesses leading to code execution on the host.
CVE-2026-123910 and CVE-2026-123911 (CVSS score of 9.8) are heap out-of-bounds write and use-after-free flaws in the I/O filter service, while CVE-2026-123912 (CVSS score of 9.3) is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the XHCI USB controller that requires local administrative privileges on a virtual machine.
An attacker “may exploit this issue to execute code as the virtual machine’s VMX process running on the host. On ESX, the exploitation is contained within the VMX sandbox whereas, on Workstation and Fusion, this may lead to code execution on the machine where Workstation or Fusion is installed,” Broadcom explains.

articles.title: OPINION: Separate the hype from reality in China’s robotics race
articles.summary:
Let’s start with the obvious; most of what you’ve seen of Chinese robots is not real. If you’re like me, your Instagram feed is full of humanoids doing backflipS or folding the laundry. The conclusion is either that China has solved robotics and we (Europe) are finished, or that they have adopted everything and we are just behind.
So we went to look. In August, six of us from Extantia visited around fifteen companies across Shanghai, Hangzhou and Beijing, then walked the floor of the World Robot Conference with its 300 exhibitors.
So, what is real?
The gap between the hype and reality

articles.title: Hope Is Not A Strategy: What First-Silicon Success Really Takes

It was also the starting point for a recent episode of ‘Wearing Flip Flops’, where host Ronen sat down with Axiomise CEO Ashish Darbari. The conversation traveled from AI silicon and power bugs to the place of formal engineers in a verification team. But one idea ran through all of it: Hope is not a strategy. Determinism is.
Here is what that idea means in practice and why we believe it matters more today than ever.
The latest Wilson Research Group functional verification study puts first-silicon success at around 5%, down from 14% in 2024. At Axiomise, that number doesn’t surprise us.
Look at who is building chips. Two years ago, the survey was shaped by a wave of new RISC-V teams, where design was moving faster than verification could follow. Today it is the turn of custom AI silicon, built not only for hyperscalers but for phones and cars too. For verification, this is an unknown territory.
Formal is in more projects than ever, perhaps 30 to 40% of them. But “using formal” can mean very different things. Data centers are getting their own natural gas power plants
The numbers behind the off-grid gas power boom.
One of the biggest roadblocks to starting up a data center is getting approval to connect to the electric grid—a wait that could last as long as a decade. Some developers aren’t willing to wait and are instead opting to build their own off-grid, or behind-the-meter, gas power plants to fuel the AI boom.
xAI’s Memphis campus has famously used dozens of natural gas turbines, some of them without permits, as far back as 2024. At the time, that facility was a rarity, and it faced scrutiny from regulators. It remains the subject of ongoing legal battles. But the strategy of going off-grid for power has since become a lot more common.
As of October 2026, data center developers have announced plans for more than 100 behind-the-meter gas power plants at facilities in the US, according to data from Cleanview, a market intelligence company. The facilities have a combined planned capacity of over 115 gigawatts, more than double the peak power demand of California. The vast majority of these announcements have come since the beginning of 2025.
It’s possible that not all these facilities will be built; only a small fraction are under construction or operating today. But there’s a growing trend of large data centers looking to build their own power supply, and this could shape the grid—and its climate impacts—for decades to come.

articles.title: We Get the Infrastructure We Pay For
articles.summary:
We Get the Infrastructure We Pay For
This essay originally appeared as part of a round table in The Free Press entitled “Is America’s Infrastructure Under Attack?”
Microsoft, the FAA, banks, United Airlines, the NSA—it’s been a really bad week in cyberspace. But, amazing as it might seem, these are not related. As far as we know, they’re not the result of cyberattacks. They’re not even related to AI. (Well, that’s mostly true. The NSA will probably never tell us what went wrong.) It’s really just a series of unfortunate coincidences.
Our computerized infrastructure is vulnerable and fragile. Much of it is old, and has been incrementally patched and upgraded. A surprising amount of it is maintained by hobbyists, without any recompense. And more and more of it is centralized: the same systems affecting many different aspects of our lives and society. In many cases, it just barely works. And when it fails, it tends to fail badly.
There are a lot of technological reasons why this is true, but they are all downstream of the economic ones. The technologies we rely on are built and maintained within our economic system—and that’s where the core problem lies.
Security, safety, resilience, redundancy, recoverability—these are all essential parts of reliable technology, but they are all costs.
More importantly, they are inefficient: costs that feel wasteful until something bad happens. Modern shareholder capitalism, and private equity in particular, squeeze all inefficiencies out of a …

articles.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted

Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists.
Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn’t enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated. On November 6, new uploads to Tidal hit a whopping 60 percent AI-generated.
As things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years. That accounts for 6.3 percent of Tidal’s total catalog. On December 9, Tidal will delete all those songs. The streamer notes this will have essentially no negative impact, because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days. Throughout its announcement, Tidal is careful to stipulate that it’s only talking about music that has been fully created by AI. Artists can still use AI tools as long as the final product contains human elements.

That picture involves solar paired with energy storage, based on an analysis Porter and his colleagues at G2VP recently conducted on the state of the data center power market.

Pero esas dos etiquetas no describen lo mismo, y conviene saber las diferencias: una habla de cómo se fermenta la masa y la otra de qué parte del cereal se ha utilizado para hacer la harina. Esto también quiere decir que puede haber panes que reunan las dos cosas.
La respuesta corta. Si buscando un pan saludable comparamos el blanco de masa madre y uno 100% integral, la balanza se inclina con bastante claridad hacia el segundo. La dietista Victoria Taylor, de la British Heart Foundation, lo explica en un artículo publicado en 2023: para el consumo habitual recomienda el pan integral antes que el de masa madre hecho con harina blanca, y esto tiene que ver con la mayor cantidad de fibra del grano entero, sin desacreditar la fermentación.

Auf Tiktok ist alles „Code Rotted“: Was der Gaming-Begriff im echten Leben beschreibt
„Code Rotted“ ist ein neuer Begriff, der es in die Jugendsprache geschafft hat. Ursprünglich stammt er aus der Gaming-Szene und beschreibt plötzlich auftretende Fehler in alten Spielen. So kann beispielsweise eine Figur, mit der man früher interagieren konnte, plötzlich nicht mehr reagieren, oder eine Tür, durch die man in der virtuellen Welt schon tausendmal hindurchgeschritten ist, bleibt dauerhaft verschlossen. Grund dafür sind oft Aktualisierungen der Plattformen, auf denen die alten Spiele laufen und dafür sorgen, dass Teile davon nicht mehr funktionieren. Die Gen Z wendet diesen Begriff allerdings inzwischen auch auf alltägliche Situationen an. So lässt sich inzwischen nahezu jedes Problem auf „verrotteten Code“ zurückführen.
So kam der „Code Rot“-Begriff zustande

articles.title: De una isla retiraron 131 gatos, y luego sucedió algo que incluso sorprendió a los científicos

En 2008, las palomas de cabeza roja de Ogasawara (un archipiélago japonés) era crítica, ya que quedaban menos de 80 ejemplares por culpa de los gatos asilvestrados que llegaron a esas islas por la acción humana. Dos años después, empezó una campaña para capturarlos que terminó con 131 gatos retirados de Chichijima, una de las islas del archipiélago, y lo curioso llegó después cuando los científicos comprobaron que las aves se recuperaban a una velocidad por encima de lo esperado.
Tres años después, los registros de palomas adultas pasaron de 111 a 966, e incluso los ejemplares más jóvenes aumentaron de 9 a 189. Se trata de un crecimiento enorme para una subespecie (Columba janthina nitens) que solo vive a unos 1.000 kilómetros del territorio principal de Japón, pero todavía queda una pregunta por resolver que va más allá de de la retirada de gatos: ¿cómo consiguieron recuperarse tan rápido?

Un equipo de la Universidad de Kioto, encabezado por Daichi Tsujimoto, decidió investigar qué estaba pasando. En un estudio publicado en Communications Biology en julio de 2025, analizaron el ADN de estas palomas y lo compararon con el de otras poblaciones emparentadas. Descubrieron que más del 80 % de su genoma presentaba homocigosidad (una señal de reproducción entre individuos emparentados), pero tenían menos mutaciones especialmente perjudiciales de las que cabría esperar.

The answer didn’t come from astronomers of the day; it was John Harrison, a self-taught carpenter and clockmaker, who developed the marine chronometer and made ocean navigation safer.
What could a prize like that help Canadian innovators solve today?
“Canada can’t grow the innovation economy with public money and regulation. It’s stifling, overly restrictive, and full of red tape.”
Fiona Simpson, BioMimir
Robert Kaul, CEO of remote patient monitoring company Cloud DX, would like to find out. In a MaRS pulse-check of 21 high-growth founders and executives looking at what it takes to scale a company in Canada, Kaul proposed putting up $100 million to incentivize startups to solve “the hardest problems the country faces,” from hospital overcrowding and lagging productivity to homelessness and substance addiction.
“The allure of a large monetary prize and ultimate prestige can generate more than 100 times [the investment],” he said.
Toronto-based MaRS Discovery District is marking 25 years as the anchor innovation hub for Canadian startups. Its fall snapshot (captured from October 23 to November 6) heard from founders and executives of 21 high-growth ventures in its portfolio. articles.title: Drupal Flaw Found by Anthropic Scanner Exploited in Attacks
articles.summary:
A recently patched Drupal core vulnerability is being exploited in the wild, according to the cybersecurity agency CISA and Drupal developers.
The vulnerability, CVE-2026-132165, can be exploited for remote code execution. It was patched on November 18, and Drupal’s advisory says in-the-wild exploitation began shortly after.
“The Security Team has received a report this was exploited on live sites as early as 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC,” Drupal noted.
The discovery of the flaw is credited to Anthropic’s OSS Scanner, a free opt-in service that regularly scans enrolled open source projects for vulnerabilities.
Anthropic has not said how many vulnerabilities OSS Scanner has found since its October launch, but as of early November, it reported disclosing more than 5,000 vulnerabilities overall, across 680 open source projects.
CISA added CVE-2026-132165 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on November 24, instructing federal agencies to address it by November 27.
No public information appears to be available on attacks exploiting CVE-2026-132165. It’s unclear how many websites are affected.
The security hole affects the installer that ships with Drupal core, which enables users to set up a new site. An unauthenticated attacker — under certain conditions — can abuse the installer to reinstall Drupal, which can allow them to hijack the website or execute arbitrary code.

articles.title: Getting a GPU is only the beginning. Ask AWS EKS.
articles.summary:
Getting a GPU is only the beginning. Ask AWS EKS.
Eight minutes is a long time to wait for another copy of an AI model to start serving traffic. It feels longer when the requests are already coming in. And while Kubernetes can schedule another replica, there’s still hardware to provision, a container image to pull, model weights to load, and GPU code to compile.
The autoscaler got the message, but the model is still getting dressed.
At KubeCon + CloudNativeCon this month in Salt Lake City, The New Stack’s Matt Burns asked Sajjan Gundapunnedi, a senior engineering manager for Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS), what developers can do in those eight minutes. Their conversation starts with the scramble to find GPUs and gets into the engineering decisions that determine how much work those GPUs actually do.
“Demand for GPU capacity or any accelerated capacity is outpacing supply everywhere,” Gundapunnedi told TNS.
Give Kubernetes more to do
In our interview, Gundapunnedi describes two ways to line up accelerated capacity through EKS Auto Mode and Karpenter, the Kubernetes node provisioner. On-Demand Capacity Reservations secure capacity in a specific Availability Zone, subject to availability. Capacity Blocks let teams book capacity for a fixed future window. That gives teams planning a training or fine-tuning run a way to schedule the job around a reservation.
“What this lets you do is faster communication for your job,” Gundapunnedi told TNS.

articles.title: Engineering Around Non-Determinism: Evals, Grounding, and Release Gates for AI-Drafted Suspicious Reports
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- A drafting agent should refuse to draft when the evidence is missing. Stopping with an explicit "insufficient context" signal is safer than a fluent narrative built around gaps.
- An LLM judge is itself non-deterministic. Freeze its version and pair it with a deterministic fact-checker for names, dates, and amounts.
- Building agentic systems on probabilistic LLMs requires engineering around them: evals, context engineering, observability, regression runs, and human-in-the-loop controls contain the effects of randomness rather than removing it.
- Grounding the system in authoritative case evidence and a knowledge-augmented graph data system helps ensure that every material claim is supported by traceable data.
- Versioned models, prompts, policies, retrieval configurations, and reviewer actions make the system observable, reversible, and suitable for regulated production environments.

Financial institutions must investigate potentially suspicious activity and prepare accurate, complete, and timely reports for Financial Intelligence Units. The process is sensitive, labor-intensive, and subject to strict deadlines. Music streaming service Tidal said on Tuesday that it will start banning and removing songs generated fully with AI in a bid to stem the flood of submissions to its platform. The company said that over the past 90 days, more than 43% of tracks uploaded to its platform were generated by AI, and that was a major reason driving this decision.
Tidal said it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year. With the new rules in place, the platform said it will be rejecting roughly 80,000-85,000 tracks per day.
Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata says they are made fully using AI.
The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.
The move comes as AI-generated music inundates streaming services across the board. Tidal is one of the first major platforms after Bandcamp to ban AI music outright. Larger platforms like Spotify and YouTube Music have adopted a milder approach to this issue, choosing to label AI-generated music instead of offering filters or taking stronger measures.

  A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.

An eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function. Researchers found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the widespread assumption that screen time is necessarily harmful to developing brains.
The findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less important than how they use that time. Activities that encourage learning, creativity, and problem-solving could be particularly valuable. Researchers emphasize that the goal should not be to eliminate screen time, but to balance it with physical activity and mentally stimulating experiences.

articles.title: Radware discloses breach exposing customer cloud access keys
articles.summary:
Cybersecurity company Radware says attackers gained access to some of its customers' account details and cloud access keys through an unsecured internal Cloud WAF (Web Application Firewall) management API that was left exposed online.
Founded in 1996 and headquartered in Tel Aviv, Radware now provides application delivery and DDoS protection services to more than 12,500 enterprise and telecom carrier customers worldwide.
In a root cause analysis report shared by an anonymous source with BleepingComputer, Radware says it blocked the originating IP address and access to the internal management API. The company also revoked and replaced all internal account credentials after detecting the breach on Thursday, ten hours after the initial unauthorized API access.
"On 19 November 2026, an unauthorized party accessed an internal-only Cloud WAF management API that was reachable from the Public Internet without requiring authentication," Radware said.
"The confirmed information potentially accessed includes customer contact details, and for a subset of customers, the credentials configured for log export into their self-managed storage (AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, or SFTP)."
The company added that the breach did not expose WAF traffic inspection, certificates, end-users’ data, customer application traffic, or cloud DDoS services and data.

articles.summary:
94% of India's most-used online platforms still use dark patterns: LocalCircles
A LocalCircles study finds that 94% of India's 354 most-used online platforms continue to deploy dark patterns, with 37 of 45 sectors having no fully compliant platform.
As many as 94% of India's most-used online platforms continue to use deceptive design practices, commonly known as dark patterns, despite growing regulatory scrutiny, according to a new study by LocalCircles.
The study analysed 354 online platforms across 45 sectors and found that only 20 were free of dark patterns. Further, 37 sectors had no platform that fully complied with the dark pattern guidelines.
The findings come weeks before the amended Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2026, take effect on January 1, 2027. Under the new rules, e-commerce companies must conduct annual self-audits and prominently display certificates declaring their platforms free of dark patterns.
Dark patterns or Dark UX are user interface designs that trick users into taking unintended actions such as buying a subscription, making payments or sharing personal data.
The study also found gaps in the self-declaration process. Of the 31 companies that had submitted a 'dark pattern free' declaration to the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), platforms operated by 23 companies, or 74%, were still found to have dark patterns. Only eight companies were found to be compliant.

articles.summary:
Four years after African founders made up roughly one in 17 companies in a Y Combinator batch, the continent has become a footnote at Demo Day. The reasons say as much about how YC has changed as about African tech.
In early-2022, Y Combinator’s Winter batch included 24 African startups, 18 of them from Nigeria. For the first time, an African country ranked third in a YC cohort, behind only the United States (US) and India. Lagos founders talked about the accelerator as a rite of passage, and the Paystack exit to Stripe made the path look repeatable.
Indeed, Disrupt Africa wrote articles around that time about the “cult of Y Combinator”, and the rave reviews the programme received from founders that participated in it.
That moment did not last. By Winter 2023 the African count had fallen to three, and Winter 2024 again admitted just three. Africa’s share of a batch had shrunk from about six per cent at the peak to around one per cent by Winter 2024. A search of the YC website for African startups for the 12 batches since then returns the message “sorry, no matching companies found”.
The pullback, however, is not a single decision made in San Francisco. It is the product of three things moving at once – a YC that has changed what it wants, an African funding market that cooled faster than most, and a portfolio record that has made the case for Africa harder to argue.
The numbers: from 24, to a handful, to none

High-level synthesis (HLS) initially struggled to find a market, but eventually it became a valuable tool for certain kinds of design. It is now threatened by the promise of AI, which some predict will allow engineers to go from specification to finished silicon while avoiding many EDA tools, including HLS.
Most developers of HLS solutions are not troubled by this today, though they do see many changes on the horizon.
HLS has been most valuable for algorithmic accelerators, although that could change. “When I have something that is too slow or power hungry to run on a CPU, I may want to look at custom silicon,” says Stuart Clubb, technical product management director at Siemens EDA. “I might choose to go the path of IP reuse, and that is the most likely answer for a bus interface or peripheral. articles.title: Palo Alto Networks Patches Fragnesia Flaw Used to Root Firewalls
articles.summary:
Palo Alto Networks on Tuesday announced PAN-OS updates that patch the Fragnesia Linux kernel vulnerability exploited to root its firewalls.
Tracked as CVE-2026-46300, Fragnesia was disclosed in May 2026 as a privilege escalation bug in the kernel’s XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem. It allows unprivileged attackers to overwrite sensitive system files to gain root permissions.
On October 26, cybersecurity firm Dream warned that a Chinese-speaking threat actor successfully exploited the critical PHP2Shell bugs and the Linux kernel weakness to hack two servers of a US government-affiliated organization.
As part of the AI-assisted campaign, the attackers compromised 25 servers (24 firewalls and one internal firewall management server), exploiting PHP2Shell to gain remote code execution (RCE), and executing a Fragnesia exploit to deploy webshells with root privileges.
On October 29, Palo Alto Networks confirmed that the threat actor hit PAN-OS firewalls with management interfaces exposed to the internet in attacks chaining PHP2Shell with Fragnesia.
By October 30, the company had released patches for PHP2Shell across all supported PAN-OS versions, closing the known initial-access path.
“If you are running a fixed PAN-OS listed in the CVE-2026-109618 [PHP2Shell] advisory, you are protected,” Palo Alto Networks notes in a Tuesday advisory.
Regardless, the company released new PAN-OS versions that address CVE-2026-46300: 12.2.4-h3, 12.1.10-h6, 12.1.7-h15, 12.1.4-h15, 11.2.16-h3, 11.2.13-h6, 1…

Car l’informatique quantique possède des propriétés uniques. En s’appuyant sur les règles qui gouvernent l'infiniment petit, là où un ordinateur classique teste les possibilités une par une, une machine quantique peut en explorer un très grand nombre en même temps. Mais il faut encore la dompter, car ses composants sont d'une grande fragilité et les erreurs de calcul sont nombreuses.
Les promesses, elles, sont immenses : découverte de médicaments, cybersécurité, logistique, finance… Pourtant, c'est vers un autre secteur, auquel on pense moins, que de nombreux regards se tournent aujourd'hui : l'énergie.
Un casse-tête permanent
Car faire fonctionner un réseau électrique est un casse-tête permanent. À chaque seconde, la production doit coller à la consommation, alors que le solaire et l'éolien varient au gré de la météo. Il faut aussi choisir quelles centrales allumer ou éteindre, et quand, pour répondre à la demande au moindre coût. Les combinaisons possibles explosent, et c'est précisément le genre de problème où le calcul quantique pourrait faire gagner un temps précieux.

articles.title: Enthusiast gets GTA V running on a 2007 Radeon with just 64MB of VRAM — config edits, Windows 8, and an overclock lift it from 1 FPS to 20 FPS, but most cars stop rendering
articles.summary:
Enthusiast gets GTA V running on a 2007 Radeon with just 64MB of VRAM — config edits, Windows 8, and an overclock lift it from 1 FPS to 20 FPS, but most cars stop rendering
GTA V’s original PC release asks for a 1GB card; this one has a sixteenth of that.
YouTube channel Budget-Builds Official has done the unthinkable, getting Grand Theft Auto V to run on a Radeon graphics card from 2007 with just 64MB of VRAM. The game is almost downright playable, too, with config edits, a move to Windows 8, and an overclock getting its speed up from just 1 FPS into the 13 to 20 FPS range, sans most cars, that is.
The channel detailed the feat, which targets a GPU with just a sixteenth of the video memory that’s usually required to play the game. GTA V Legacy lists, as its minimum, an Nvidia 9800 GT or AMD HD 4870, both cards with DirectX 10 support and 1GB of VRAM. The Enhanced version, released in 2025, needs 4GB, from a GTX 1630 or RX 6400 as specified.
In fact, the chosen card, an ATI Radeon HD 2350, is potentially the worst card that can launch GTA V, at least by the tester’s claim, even though its DDR2 memory is probably one of the few types not in short supply at the moment. Notably, this approach doesn’t involve using a unified or shared system memory AMD APU workaround; this is dedicated VRAM. It’s also not the first attempt at something like this, as the channel has an earlier run with 8MB of VRAM on games like Half-Life 2 and Minecraft.

articles.title: Amazon drone crashes on garage after delivering shampoo, draws FAA probe
articles.summary:
An Amazon delivery drone that clipped a fiber-optic line before crashing onto a garage roof is now the subject of an investigation by the US Federal Aviation Administration. It’s the latest delivery drone mishap caught on video as Amazon and other companies are ramping up such aerial delivery operations across the United States.
The November 20 incident began with Jim Brennan and his wife, residents of Huntington Woods, Michigan, placing an order for shampoo and being surprised by a notification about the package arriving by drone within seven minutes, according to WXYZ 7 News Detroit. After the drone dropped the package into Brennan’s backyard, it lost a propeller when it caught on fiber-optic cable and floundered sideways before getting pinned between the neighbor’s garage roof and some power lines.
“Like a sick bird, it tried to go up, it tried to get out of here,” Brennan told WXYZ 7.
Amazon Prime Air currently operates a fleet of battery-powered MK30 drones that can deliver packages weighing up to five pounds and have onboard sense-and-avoid technology to avoid obstacles. However, the drone clearly failed to avoid the thin fiber-optic cable in this case—so hopefully the FAA investigation would take that into account along with Amazon delivery drone procedures.
The FAA preliminary accident and incident notification briefly describes the incident as “UAS struck a fiber cable, a residential garage, and became entangled in power lines during takeoff.” That notice was posted …

articles.title: As MCP turns two, Claude gets Skills over MCP and better support for long-running tasks
articles.summary:
As MCP turns two, Claude gets Skills over MCP and better support for long-running tasks
Anthropic on Tuesday marked the second anniversary of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) by bringing support for skills, long-running tasks, and file uploads over MCP to Claude.
Skills over MCP, which lets MCP servers publish skills alongside their tools, is now available in public beta, while Tasks, which first landed in Claude Code as a beta in October, and Elicitation are now generally available. File uploads will roll out soon.
All three are meant to help agents work more autonomously and for longer stretches of time, which, according to the protocol’s maintainers, is also where the project focused much of its second year. In its announcement, Anthropic says these features let Claude treat an MCP server more like another agent that it can learn from and delegate work to.
Den Delimarsky, a lead maintainer of MCP at Anthropic, tells The New Stack, “You have long-running tasks, you have events, you have file uploads and downloads, you have skills over MCP, and all of them working together now enable a completely different spectrum of scenarios.”
From early adoption to agents
When Anthropic first launched MCP in November 2024, it wasn’t clear whether the protocol would pan out, says David Soria Parra, who co-created MCP at Anthropic and remains one of its lead maintainers. That first year was mostly about adoption, he says.

articles.title: Ladybird is the first new browser engine in years, and of course some sites are broken
articles.summary:
First look: Ladybird, an independent web browser running on a rendering engine its developers wrote from scratch, is now available for alpha testing on macOS and Linux. Developer Andreas Kling announced the release Monday after more than four years of work. It is the first browser in years not to run on Gecko, Blink, or WebKit, the three engines behind today's most popular browsers.
Most browser makers start from an existing engine and build features on top of it. Ladybird's team wrote its own, so every part of the browser, from how pages are laid out to how they are drawn on screen, comes from code the project controls instead of code it inherited.
Ladybird started as part of a C++ project, but its developers later began porting the code to Rust using AI. That means testers are getting a codebase that is partway through a move from one language to another, with AI tools helping with the rewrite.
For engineers, this makes Ladybird a live test of whether AI-assisted porting can work at the scale of a full browser engine.
Kling is candid about the browser's current limitations. In his announcement, he said the browser built around the Ladybird engine "is modest but functional." He also warned that "some websites won't work" during the alpha. A new engine has a lot of ground to cover before it can handle the full range of sites people use every day, and the alpha is meant to show where it still falls short.
