articles.title: Exein launches Ray AI agent to show manufacturers which firmware weaknesses to fix first
articles.summary:
Exein launches Ray AI agent to show manufacturers which firmware weaknesses to fix first
Italian physical artificial intelligence cybersecurity company Exein SpA today launched an AI agent called Ray that it claims can help manufacturers find the security weaknesses that matter most in their connected-device firmware.
Ray is built into Exein Analyzer, the company’s firmware security platform, which examines firmware for vulnerabilities, security weaknesses and compliance issues. Engineers can then use Ray to explore those findings in a conversational way, looking at the security posture of a single product or an entire fleet.
The new offering is designed to address a growing security gap for manufacturers. Some connected products contain thousands of software components, and a single scan of one can flag hundreds of potential issues, Exein said. Which of those weaknesses actually needs to be fixed first is said to be the harder question.
Rather than working through separate vulnerability lists, security scores, trackers and compliance reports, engineers can put questions to Ray about Analyzer’s findings. Among the questions engineers can ask are what is driving a product’s security score, which vulnerabilities need attention first and which compliance issues affect a firmware image.

AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
- Date:

- Source:

Researchers found that even AI models that closely predict brain activity may rely on internal processes the brain doesn't use, raising important questions about their reliability in neuroscience research.
- Share:
Artificial intelligence may be much less like the human brain than scientists have long assumed. A new study from York University has uncovered a surprising weakness in AI models that are widely used to understand how the brain processes visual information.
For years, researchers have relied on artificial neural networks (ANNs), computer systems designed to perform tasks such as recognizing objects in images, to investigate how vision works. Over the past decade, these models have become some of the leading tools for explaining the brain's visual system. Their ability to reproduce patterns of brain activity has made them especially valuable in neuroscience.
But the new findings raise an important question: Just because AI can successfully imitate certain responses in the brain, does that mean it actually processes visual information in the same way?

articles.title: 9 startups picked for 1st Africa Ignite climate adaptation cohort
articles.summary:
The United Nations Industrial Development Organisation (UNIDO) and BFA Global have selected nine climate adaptation startups from eight African countries for the first cohort of the Africa Ignite programme.
Funded by the Adaptation Fund Climate Innovation Accelerator (AFCIA) and run under the Adaptation SME Innovation Facility (ASIF), Ignite targets early-stage startups that have built a working prototype but are yet to validate it with users. The nine were chosen from 453 applications.
Over eight weeks, founders will test their solutions with farmers, cooperatives and agribusinesses. Weekly live sessions, specialist office hours, AI training and real-world user testing will help them gather evidence of demand and impact, sharpen their business models, and prepare to land customers and raise investment.
“Every founder in this cohort has a working prototype. The next step is often the hardest: putting it in front of a cassava farmer, a coffee cooperative or a poultry producer and learning what they will use and pay for,” said Rasima Swarup, ASIF lead at BFA Global.
The cohort includes Benin’s ALLO VETO, which helps poultry farmers formulate affordable feed from local ingredients when drought disrupts supply; Angolan biodigester maker EcoBioGás; and Tanzania’s GeoVLUP Adaptation Services, which turns farm and climate data into practical guidance for coffee farmers.

articles.title: Why AI Struggles To Reuse Chip Designs
articles.summary:
AI can accelerate derivative designs, but physical constraints and incomplete data limit how much can be automated.
Key Takeaways:
- AI can accelerate derivative chip design, but those derivatives may not be physically viable or cost-effective.
- AI-assisted reuse depends on the availability of accurate design data, engineering knowledge, and proven methodologies.
- End-to-end automation is limited by gaps in multi-physics simulation, implementation, and verification.
Chipmakers are seeing mixed results when they apply AI to derivative and new chip designs, finding that AI-generated solutions can be substantially different and more costly than expected, and that AI-driven designs introduce new manufacturing and verification challenges.
Several key problems have emerged when incorporating AI in chip design. Among them:
- The data needed to ensure that follow-on designs will function as expected may not be complete because some of that data resides in other companies, such as foundries, OSATs, and various equipment and process providers;
- Integrating rapidly evolving AI capabilities into established EDA flows remains challenging, especially where predictability, traceability, and silicon-proven results are required.
- Many organizations have customized tools for their own chips, markets, and expertise, and AI tools have not yet adapted to those changes.

articles.title: Back-to-back measles deaths is our new reality; US tally now at 14
articles.summary:
Last week, international health authorities formally announced that the US had lost its measles-elimination status, meaning that the virus is once again endemic. But the official determination is a bit like getting the technical readout of a cracked dam while the country is already feet under water.
The national tally of measles cases is nearing 6,000 for the year, the highest count since 1991. Transmission is widespread, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases. There have been 43 outbreaks this year, which account for 96 percent of the cases. Four states have case counts above 500, including Pennsylvania, which leads with 1,638 cases as of November 23. Nearly 650 people have been hospitalized nationwide. As of today, 14 people have died.
Deaths and transmission
On November 23, Pennsylvania’s health department announced its ninth confirmed death, an unvaccinated resident of Centre County. On November 24, Wisconsin reported its third measles death, an adult in Lafayette County. The report follows two other deaths in the state, an infant and a child. New York has also reported a death, which was of a 7-month-old baby. On November 20, Virginia reported the death of a child between the age of 0 and 4.

While a larger operator could pool infrastructure, reduce duplicated investment and strengthen its capacity to finance expensive next-generation networks, absorbing Telkom would also remove an independent infrastructure competitor. articles.title: What’s going on with the Riemann hypothesis?
articles.summary:
Last week, news broke that a mathematician had used AI to help crack one of the biggest outstanding problems in math: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis. The news follows several other major breakthroughs in math that have either been enabled by or managed entirely by large language model-based systems, a development that has left the entire field of mathematics in a state of upset.
It’s too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it. But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math.
Tackling Riemann
The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by (you will be surprised to learn) Bernhard Riemann. There’s not an obvious way to describe the details of the actual hypothesis simply, but it has implications for the distribution of prime numbers. This gives it significance for areas ranging from number theory to cryptography. As Wikipedia accurately states, “It is considered by pure mathematicians to be one of the most important problems in the field.”
The proof of the hypothesis was announced by a mathematician named Levent Alpöge, who has been working at Anthropic, and, not surprisingly, used Claude to generate it. His announcement is written in a somewhat florid style (example: “one of which was already new and shocking, making very simple one of the shadows of Riemann over which we mathematicians felt most triumph”), and he has apparently dropped some …

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Unpatched Flaw in Defunct Idunno AntiCsrf Library
articles.summary:
Threat actors are exploiting an unpatched vulnerability in the open source anti-CSRF library Idunno AntiCsrf for remote code execution (RCE), security researchers warn.
AntiCsrf is a legacy ASP.NET module for WebForms applications that has no active maintainer and is no longer actively supported. The most recent version, 0.9.1 Beta, was released in December 2008.
Tracked as CVE-2026-131914 (CVSS score of 9.3), the exploited security defect is described as an insecure deserialization bug in the processing of HTTP POST requests to ASP.NET WebForms endpoints.
“Exploitation requires only a single HTTP POST request with no prior authentication or valid CSRF token. Active exploitation in the wild has been observed,” Google Cloud’s Mandiant warned on November 18.
The flaw allows an attacker to supply any non-empty value in the CSRF cookie along with a Base64-encoded gadget chain to gain RCE in the context of the IIS worker process, Mandiant notes.
According to preemptive cybersecurity firm WatchTowr, the issue exists because AntiCsrf does not perform sufficient checks on data from incoming form submissions before reconstructing it into program objects.
“The vulnerable check runs before the application’s own page logic, so it can affect many pages on an affected site, not just ones that use a login form. A successful attack gives the attacker control over the process that runs the website, which can lead to full compromise of the server,” WatchTowr says.

The country says that unless these companies take reasonable steps to protect users from harmful content and addictive features on their platforms, they could be fined up to 5% of their global revenue.
Australia's Labor government struck a deal with the Greens on Tuesday that gives its Digital Duty of Care bill the support it needs to pass the Senate. The original proposal capped fines at A$109.2 million, or about US$72 million. But even that amount looks modest next to what a company the size of Meta could face under the revised bill.

The changes would also give Australians who suffer harm the right to sue a platform directly, opening the door to class actions. The new approach uses AI to examine electronic health records, searching for combinations of symptoms, medical conditions, risk factors, and healthcare activity that might otherwise be overlooked. By recognizing these patterns, researchers hope to make bladder cancer screening more accurate and help doctors find the disease when treatment is most likely to succeed.

articles.title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando
articles.summary:
OpenAI has detailed Pando, a new backend that scales Git for concurrent coding-agent workloads without replacing familiar Git workflows. The company reports nearly 80% lower median push latency by coordinating branch updates independently and reusing stored packfiles across fetches.
Pando now powers all development in OpenAI's monorepo and is serving nearly a petabyte of Git data per day. OpenAI attributes the increased load to Codex-driven development, and each push can in turn trigger multiple CI jobs that all fetch the same history. Pando went into production in April 2026.
Rather than replace Git's client and protocol, OpenAI has changed how the backend coordinates reference updates and stores and transfers objects. On a push, Pando validates the incoming packfile as it's being streamed to immutable blob storage, without unpacking it into a local repository. A metadata transaction records the reference version (containing the new branch tip, the packfile and its dependencies on earlier reference versions) and atomically updates the reference pointer. Updates to unrelated references can proceed independently of one another; updates to the same reference still need to be coordinated.
OpenAI refers to this as causal consistency with serialisable updates to individual references and read-your-own-write consistency. A reader gets the history needed for the requested revision, but fetching a number of branches won't provide a repository-wide snapshot. Two clients can see differ…

The gang surfaced on November 17, claiming seven victims on its extortion site, including chip maker AMD, PepsiCo, Cigna Healthcare, AutoZone, and Lucid Motors, but none of them have publicly confirmed a data breach.
However, cybersecurity company ReversingLabs has been tracking Inception gang's activity and says that it has been operating since late October.
The security firm has confirmed the existence of 21 domains used for SSO phishing, 41 domains believed to be used in campaign infrastructure, and 4 other domains with suspected use.
The researchers identified an extensive phishing infrastructure impersonating dozens of major corporations, including Dropbox, Duolingo, Western Union, Indeed, Activision Blizzard, Riot Games, Twitch, Reddit, Nestlé, Anthropic, Nintendo, Starbucks, McDonald's, Paramount, and NBCUniversal.
The existence of these domains is not proof that those firms have been breached, or even targeted yet, and none have recently disclosed cyberattacks or other related incidents.

articles.title: Jensen Huang revient à la tête de Nvidia : comment expliquer ce retournement de situation ?
articles.summary:
Ce lundi 23 novembre, nous avons assisté à un rebondissement assez inattendu : Jensen Huang a récupéré son poste de PDG au sein de Nvidia, alors qu’il avait remis sa démission 11 jours auparavant à la suite d’affaires extraconjugales, notamment avec Alice Huang, suspectée par Washington d’être une espionne au service de la Chine. Mais comment expliquer ce retour alors que le conseil d’administration de l’entreprise avait clairement annoncé que cela n’arriverait pas, tout en entamant les démarches pour trouver un remplaçant ? Si nous ne savons pas exactement ce qu’il s’est passé en coulisse, plusieurs éléments permettent d’expliquer la situation.
Donald Trump a soutenu le retour de Jensen Huang
Cela n’est pas un secret : Jensen Huang et Donald Trump affichent une certaine complicité. Nvidia a par exemple donné 25 millions de dollars (environ 23 millions d’euros) pour financer la construction de la salle de bal de la Maison-Blanche (Apple et Google ont également fait un don de plus de 20 millions de dollars). En septembre dernier, en pleine conférence, Donald Trump a appelé Jensen pour rappeler une nouvelle fois sa volonté de ne pas freiner la course à l’intelligence artificielle. Les deux hommes avaient alors montré leur plein accord.
Et nous n’allons pas parler des termes utilisés par Trump pour qualifier Jensen Huang : « une légende », « un génie », « Le meilleur atout pour l’entreprise [Nvidia], mais aussi pour les États-Unis. », etc. Bref, Donald Trump avait tout intérêt à…

articles.title: Threads comes to iPad and takes a page from X's playbook with cashtags
articles.summary:
It may have taken 15 years for Instagram to launch on the iPad, but Instagram’s other app, Threads, has taken a slightly faster path to the Apple tablet. In an overnight update, the company rolled out a big-screen version of the X competitor. It’s also added another new feature, borrowed from X: the stock-tracking feature known as cashtags.
While the iPad version of the app works well in portrait orientation, some users are disappointed to find that the landscape layout doesn’t work as they’d expect. Instead of offering a multi-column interface as on Threads’ web app, the iPad app focuses on the user’s main feed in a single-column layout. There are also options to swipe right and left from the main screen to access the search screen and the feeds menu, respectively.
The iPad app isn’t the company’s only update in the latest release. According to a post from Threads engineer Guy Dickinson, Threads will now support cashtags — a feature popularized by Twitter years ago for tracking live stock information. These specialized tags start with the dollar sign (“$”) followed by a ticker symbol. When you click on a cashtag, you can follow the discussions around the stock.
In addition, Threads is adding live stock quotes, charts, and other context at the top of each cashtag’s page. As you search for a particular cashtag, the autocomplete search results will display the stock’s current price and the percentage it’s up or down. articles.title: Kenya’s Cloud9 acquires Canadian money services business Monix Pay
articles.summary:
Kenyan digital bank Cloud9, which enables cross-border payments and borderless banking for African consumers and businesses, has acquired Canadian money services business Monix Pay to expand into North America.
Disrupt Africa reported in October 2025 on the launch of Cloud9, a digital bank enabling instant global payments, borderless banking and modern financial tools for a new generation of African consumers and businesses.
The startup recently secured an undisclosed investment from crypto and fintech accelerator Alliance, taking total funding to date to US$1 million, and it has now acquired Monix Pay, a Canadian money services business registered with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), the country’s financial intelligence and anti-money-laundering regulator.
The deal sees Cloud9 expand into North America for the first time, and means it is now registered to provide foreign exchange (FX) services, money transfers, general payment services, and virtual currency and digital asset transactions. It is a key step in the startup’s long-term plan to own the regulated infrastructure its customers depend on, rather than fully renting it from intermediaries.
“Every African business that trades globally pays a hidden tax on every transaction – in fees, in FX and in time,” said Tesh Mbaabu, founder and CEO of Cloud9. “Acquiring Monix Pay means we no longer entirely depend on others’ rails to serve our customers. We’re building the regulated infra…

articles.title: GTA 6 hace historia en PS5 y se convierte en el lanzamiento más exitoso de PlayStation
articles.summary:
Grand Theft Auto 6 no para de crecer. A pocos días de que llegara al mercado, el juego de Rockstar Games batió todos los récords de ventas, preventas y ya superó en ganancias a la taquilla de las películas más exitosas de Hollywood. Ahora, GTA 6 logró convertirse en el lanzamiento más exitoso de la historia de PlayStation, impulsando la venta de consolas.
De acuerdo con el blog oficial de PlayStation, más de 39 millones de usuarios han jugado GTA 6 en PS5 desde su lanzamiento. El juego también estableció un récord por el mayor número de jugadores simultáneos que ha tenido un solo título en las consolas PlayStation, superando incluso los récords en otros títulos multijugador o free-to-play, que normalmente lideran en este apartado.
Según Sony, los jugadores de GTA 6 en PS5 acumularon más de 683 millones de horas de juego entre el día de estreno y el 22 de noviembre. Cada uno ha pasado una media de 17,4 horas explorando el estado de Leonida durante los primeros días desde su lanzamiento.
Estas cifras superan a cualquier otro juego de consola en los últimos años, incluyendo aquellos de los estudios first party de Sony. Si bien no hay datos oficiales, juegos como Marvel's Spider-Man 2 o God of War Ragnarök tuvieron un lanzamiento importante, aunque no al nivel de GTA 6. Otro juego que podría colarse en la comparativa es Fortnite, que se convirtió en un fenómeno cultural entre 2018 y 2019, registrando millones de jugadores concurrentes.

Jensen Huang regresó a la sede de Nvidia en Santa Clara, California, y se paró frente a cientos de empleados en el atrio para, antes de recibir aplausos, pedir perdón. “Cometí errores muy graves y voy a trabajar para recuperarme”, dijo el cofundador y presidente ejecutivo, reinstalado por unanimidad el lunes 23 de noviembre tras 11 días fuera del cargo. Comenzó con un chiste —“Este es mi primer día de trabajo; no tengo computadora, así que el departamento de IT me va a dar una nueva”— pero enseguida cambió el tono. “Lo siento muchísimo por haberlos hecho pasar por todo esto. Cometí errores muy graves”, dijo. Las imágenes fueron compartidas originalmente por Ming-Yu Liu, vicepresidente de investigación de Nvidia, en X. Luego agradeció la segunda oportunidad y prometió ser “un mejor CEO esta vez”. El video se volvió viral en pocas horas.

articles.title: ¿Tu PC va más lento? Este ajuste de Chrome podría estar consumiendo RAM sin que lo sepas
articles.summary:
El consumo de memoria ha sido el talón de Aquiles de Chrome durante muchos años y las cosas no parecen mejorar. El navegador de Google nuevamente vuelve al centro de la polémica luego de que se descubriera que consume una cantidad grosera de RAM tras cerrarlo. Este comportamiento es relativamente nuevo y está relacionado con la integración de Gemini.
Un usuario descubrió que Chrome puede consumir hasta 700 MB de RAM después de cerrarlo. En una publicación en Reddit, el usuario detalló que, tras cerrar el navegador de la forma habitual, el Administrador de Tareas de Windows mantenía varios procesos de chrome.exe ejecutándose en segundo plano. Estas tareas consumían entre 300 MB y 700 MB de RAM, por lo que el usuario tenía que cerrarlas de forma manual.
Las tareas de Chrome o de cualquier otro navegador basado en Chromium que se mantienen en segundo plano son un mal que lleva años. La mayoría de las veces se trata de un ajuste en la configuración relacionado con las aplicaciones o extensiones, pero en esta ocasión era diferente. El usuario dijo que probó de todo, incluyendo un borrado de caché, cookies y deshabilitando todos los complementos.
Tras restaurar la configuración de Chrome, el usuario encontró que el problema estaba relacionado con una opción ligada al perfil. La integración de Gemini en Chrome activa dos funciones que mantienen al asistente de IA funcionando todo el tiempo. articles.title: Microsoft’s historic cloud outage exposed an engineering “fog of war”
articles.summary:
According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters, Microsoft has declared a “Code Red” overhaul of its engineering response practices after the November 12 outage that lost access to Exchange Online, Teams, and Outlook for users worldwide.
Per the memos, Microsoft 365 Core President Jason Henderson described the outage as having the most customer impact in the history of Exchange Online. In a separate memo, Henderson wrote that an urgent production fix in a recent incident took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. Microsoft’s target for its most urgent security fixes is to move from detection to safe worldwide deployment in one hour. “Needless to say, we aren’t here yet,” Henderson wrote.
The memos, which Reuters reviewed but Microsoft has not published, outline the response to the November 12 disruption. The company’s post-incident report, dated November 20, attributed the downtime to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July, which caused lock contention in the gateway processes. A Teams traffic failover then dumped additional load onto infrastructure already under stress, as maintenance had left nearly 14 percent of gateway server capacity offline at the time of the incident.

articles.title: Vancouver considering stricter rules, oversight for AI data centres
articles.summary:
Vancouver City Council has unanimously directed City of Vancouver staff to examine stronger oversight of new data centres, including third-party assessments of their effects on the surrounding area, public reporting on their operations, and ways to secure benefits for local residents.
OneCity city councillor Lucy Maloney’s member motion, approved last week after amendments, asks City staff to develop recommendations on how the municipal government should assess and regulate data centres as artificial intelligence (AI) facilities grow.
“This is about ensuring we move forward responsibly and thoughtfully. As we’ve seen in the United States, hyperscale data centres can bring significant challenges. Compared to many other industrial businesses, data centres are often far more resource intensive, placing greater strain on public infrastructure. They can consume vast quantities of water and energy while producing pollution, waste heat, and noise. They also tend to create fewer jobs than other industrial uses of the land,” said Maloney during the City Council meeting.
“Furthermore, the economic benefits to host communities often fall short of the returns realised by investors by a long shot. This is a global issue, not just limited to the U.S. Cities worldwide are sharing best practices to develop effective frameworks and ensure data centres represent the best use of valuable land,” continued Maloney.

articles.title: Verra raises $5M to help consulting firms forget their institutional amnesia
articles.summary:
Verra raises $5M to help consulting firms forget their institutional amnesia
Verra, an artificial intelligence startup building the institutional memory layer for consulting firms, said today it has raised $5 million in seed funding to help those companies overcome their amnesia and make their decades of knowledge accessible to every employee.
Today’s round was led by Kearny Jackson and saw participation from Andreessen Horowitz’s a16z Speedrun, Petra and a number of strategic investors. It comes just seven months after Verra, officially known as Lighthouse Software Technologies Inc., launched its platform.
Verra was founded last year by Chief Executive Kashyap Nathan (pictured, right), who previously worked as a researcher at OpenAI Group PBC and Palantir Technologies Inc., and Christopher Farrington (left), a former software engineer at Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Ltd. In an interview, Nathan explained that he and Farrington had seen firsthand how well-paid consultants would struggle with new customer engagements, wasting hours of time researching to surface institutional knowledge that their company already possessed.
“Consulting firms sit on decades of proposals, models and reports, and almost none of it is usable by the people who need it next,” Nathan said. “We built the layer that makes that knowledge usable, and we built it to run inside the firm’s own cloud, because no consulting firm is going to send client work to a shared service.”

articles.title: Xbox Helix started as a PC in disguise, with free multiplayer and Steam, until plans changed
articles.summary:
What we know so far: Microsoft has confirmed that the next Xbox, codenamed Helix, will support PC games, but the extent of that support remains unclear. Current messaging indicates a console-first experience, but rumors suggest the project initially leaned in a much more PC-centric direction. It remains uncertain how much Microsoft's current roadmap resembles that original plan.
Sources tell Windows Central that, before Asha Sharma became Xbox CEO earlier this year, Microsoft planned for its next console to essentially be a PC with an Xbox-style UI and support for Xbox console games. This would have required the company to drop its online multiplayer paywall.
As prior rumors suggested, the Asus ROG Xbox Ally was a rough draft of the experience the Xbox division intended for its next console while under Phil Spencer. The next Xbox would have run on Windows and booted into Microsoft's new Xbox Mode by default, but users could exit to the traditional desktop and install any Windows app, including Steam.
Microsoft's official messaging remains vague but implies the opposite approach while retaining some PC compatibility. The company recently described its next console, now codenamed Helix, as a console that plays PC games, not a PC that plays console games.

articles.title: Move fast, don’t break 100 apps: Dan Garfield on keeping AI-powered coding on the rails
articles.summary:
Move fast, don’t break 100 apps: Dan Garfield on keeping AI-powered coding on the rails
An AI coding agent can give a product manager a working prototype before the next planning meeting. Which is great! But someone still has to decide whether any interactions make sense, the new features solve a problem, or — most importantly — whether the team can ship it safely.
At Octopus Deploy, that’s changing how product managers pitch new features. The company is asking them to bring a prototype in place of a written requirements document and keep refining how the feature works, says Dan Garfield, its VP of Open Source. A developer can then take it the rest of the way to production.
“The ultimate differentiator now seems to be care, attention to detail, and taste.”
“The ultimate differentiator now seems to be care, attention to detail, and taste,” Garfield told The New Stack’s Matt Burns at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon this month in Salt Lake City. articles.summary:
Strange new materials can crawl, walk, and dig like living creatures
- Date:
  November 23, 2026
- Source:
  Universiteit van Amsterdam
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed remarkable materials that can crawl, walk, and dig using their own internal energy, potentially paving the way for a new generation of autonomous soft robots. They also discovered that making individual components more active can paradoxically make the entire material less responsive, challenging a long-standing principle of engineering.
- Share:
Most materials simply react when something pushes, pulls, or bends them. But a very different category of matter can draw on its own energy to change shape and respond to outside forces in surprising ways. Known as active matter, these unusual materials are attracting growing scientific interest. Now, physicists from the universities of Amsterdam, New South Wales, and Cambridge have uncovered remarkable new behaviors that could change how future machines and robots are designed.
Everyday materials such as metal, concrete, glass, and rubber are generally considered passive. They can stretch, bend, shift, or change shape when forces act on them, but the energy needed to produce those changes comes from outside the material.

articles.title: CNCF Research Shows Virtual Machines Remain Central as AI Workloads Evolve
articles.summary:
Virtual machines (VMs) continue to account for a substantial share of cloud-native production infrastructure, despite the widespread adoption of containers and Kubernetes. New research from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) and Linux Foundation Research finds that VMs host an average of 53% of production applications, while emerging AI and agentic workloads are creating additional demand for virtualisation, particularly where stronger execution isolation is required.
The report surveyed 492 cloud-native practitioners and technology leaders in September 2026. Among organisations expanding their VM footprint, 34% identified AI and agentic workloads as a contributing factor. The findings suggest that rather than replacing virtual machines with containers, organisations are increasingly combining the two to accommodate different application and security requirements.
The research challenges the assumption that cloud-native adoption necessarily means moving away from virtual machines. While containers provide portability and efficient application packaging, VMs continue to offer isolation and support for workloads that depend on dedicated operating systems or established virtualisation environments.
The survey found that 51% of respondents run at least half of their production applications on VMs. This rises to an average of 64% in organisations with more than 10,000 employees, compared with 45% among organisations with fewer than 500 employees.

articles.title: A medida que Xbox cumple 25 años, la CEO Asha Sharma dice: 'Pronto una sola persona podrá ejercer capacidades que antes requerían naciones enteras'.
articles.summary:
Cuando Microsoft lanzó Microsoft Adventure en 1979, la empresa apenas tenía 13 empleados y uno de ellos, Gordon Letwin, se encargó de adaptar aquel juego de aventuras de texto. Casi medio siglo después, hay videojuegos que necesitan cientos de desarrolladores y presupuestos de cientos de millones de dólares. Asha Sharma ha recuperado esa diferencia con motivo del 25 aniversario de Xbox, aunque no precisamente para celebrar lo mucho que ha crecido la industria: la CEO considera que desarrollar grandes juegos se ha vuelto demasiado caro y arriesgado.
En una carta publicada en Xbox Wire, Sharma reconoce que muchas ideas nunca llegan a convertirse en videojuegos y que otros proyectos terminan lejos de lo que sus creadores habían imaginado. Durante décadas, explica, la ambición de un estudio dependía del dinero, las personas y los recursos que podía reunir. Ahora cree que esa relación está empezando a romperse, hasta el punto de que “una sola persona pronto podrá disponer de capacidades que antes requerían naciones enteras”.

articles.title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security
articles.summary:
The U.K. government’s cybersecurity unit says it has seen a “marked rise” in AI-driven cyberattacks in recent months, as hackers increasingly rely on autonomous hacking tools to identify and exploit simple weaknesses to break into systems and networks.
The U.K. National Cybersecurity Center (NCSC) said it has seen several cyber incidents since September involving autonomous hacking tools, such as penetration testing tools used by defenders to stress-test their cybersecurity defenses. These incidents have caused intrusions at organizations and resulted in downtime, the unit said in a blog post.
The NCSC says that while none of the vulnerabilities being exploited are new, the speed at which these AI tools are able to carry out simple hacks has changed.
The rise in AI-related cyberattacks coincides with the broader release earlier this year of open source autonomous penetration testing tools like Artex and Cairn, among others, which anyone can download and use at no cost. The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation recently warned that malicious hackers are using AI penetration testing tools to carry out cyberattacks at unprecedented speeds.
While cyberattacks and intrusions are on the rise, the message from London is that many of these attacks are preventable with basic cybersecurity defenses and best practices.

Para Cook, esos enfrentamientos no son creados por los dispositivos o las plataformas: reflejan tensiones humanas que la tecnología puede amplificar. articles.summary:
Two of NASA’s four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks.
The missions affected by the outages—hopefully temporary—are NASA’s Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water. Odyssey arrived in orbit around Mars in 2001, and is the longest-lived Mars mission in history.
Losing its voice
The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover’s communications system. The rover has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications with a fleet of orbiters that relay data to Earth. A separate X-band system is available for direct-to-Earth communications at a lower data rate.
One of the rover’s two UHF radios was unresponsive when it powered up on October 30, triggering an automatic switch to the backup radio and placing the rover in safe mode. Ground teams at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California later discovered the backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output, NASA said in a statement last week.
“The team has stopped using both radios until they can evaluate potential causes of the issues and one or both are deemed safe to resume operating,” NASA said.

She stated that anything requiring consistent outputs for the same inputs, such as access control, configuration resolution, and data correctness guarantees, should remain within the realm of proper systems. We should definitely build the systems where we want guarantees and guardrails.

À peine sorti sur consoles, GTA 6 fait déjà des infidélités à ses plateformes d’origine. Tandis que les joueurs PC doivent composer avec le silence de Rockstar Games qui n’a toujours pas officialisé de portage sur ordinateur, la scène underground semble bien décidée à court-circuiter le calendrier du studio. Comme le rapporte le site spécialisé Gizmochina, un exécutable issu de la version Xbox de la superproduction de Rockstar a rapidement fuité en ligne après la sortie du jeu, ouvrant une brèche pour faire tourner le titre sur PC.

Trois heures pour franchir l’écran de démarrage sur PC
À l’origine de cette fuite se trouve le groupe baptisé Cyberleek, qui avait déjà mis en ligne de nombreuses fuites du jeu avant sa sortie. Le groupe a publié l’exécutable Xbox de GTA 6 afin de compléter un premier lot de fichiers qui circulait déjà sous le manteau. articles.title: Jimmy Wales, fundador de Wikipedia y premio Xataka Leyenda 2026: "Le caigo bien a la gente y los tech bros no suelen caer bien"
articles.summary:
Jimmy Wales llega a las oficinas de Webedia solo, sin asistentes, ataviado con un jersey de cuello alto y una mochila. Acaba de llegar a Madrid para recoger el premio Xataka Leyenda 2026 y no desprende la grandilocuencia que otras figuras de la tecnología sí se esfuerzan en proyectar. Al fin y al cabo, Jimmy Wales tan solo fundó la Wikipedia, una de las mayores obras colectivas de la humanidad y una de las innovaciones tecnológicas más duraderas de internet.
El contraste entre su legado y su figura es llamativo y él es consciente. Los Premios Xataka se celebran esa misma noche, pero nosotros nos sentamos a mediodía, en la Arena de Webedia, a charlar tranquilamente durante 40 minutos. Me interesa su visión sobre el futuro del conocimiento, de la Wikipedia, de la IA y sobre las decisiones personales que le han llevado a ser quien es. Se abre una Coca-Cola, el equipo de producción nos da paso y comenzamos a hablar.
Puedes ver la entrevista completa en nuestro YouTube.
"Siempre digo que soy un optimista patológico, siempre pienso que todo está bien, así que necesito pesimistas alrededor para recordarme que no todo va bien", me explica. La afirmación me sorprende. Navegando hoy en día por internet, cuesta entrever optimismo: las constantes amenazas sobre el fin de la humanidad, la ruptura de las comunidades digitales, la fuerte desconfianza hacia las instituciones. Vivimos tiempos pesimistas.
Wales es consciente de ello. Su primer libro, publicado en octubre de 2025, se titula Las…

Trabaja casi toda la semana, pero consigue ahorrar buena parte del sueldo
Y aunque sus gastos estén cubiertos en unas pocas horas, Mario no dedica el resto de la semana a descansar. De hecho, reconoce que durante estas campañas trabaja prácticamente todos los días y que el esfuerzo físico es considerable. «Trabajo como un esclavo», comenta al hablar de unas jornadas que le permiten acumular dinero para sus proyectos y futuros viajes.

Su idea es sencilla: gastar lo menos posible mientras dura el trabajo y guardar buena parte de lo que cobra. articles.title: Anthropic shares fall below IPO price, a worrying sign for AI startups
articles.summary:
Anthropic’s stock fell below its IPO price of $83, trading as low as $76 a share by midday Tuesday, down nearly 12% from Monday’s close.
Falling below the IPO price is often seen as a negative signal because underwriters typically price offerings at a discount to their expected trading value.
The AI industry has been eagerly watching how Anthropic’s shares trade, with VCs and other observers saying its performance could serve as a barometer for how public market investors value the sector.
The dramatic slump comes less than a week after Anthropic debuted on Nasdaq at $111.50 a share. If its shares continue to trade poorly in the coming weeks, the slide could put pressure on private startup valuations and weaken IPO prospects for other AI companies.
Anthropic isn’t the only AI stock selling off on Tuesday. Nvidia fell more than 7% by midday, giving back some of the more than 30%-plus gain it posted Monday after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO.

articles.title: Please don’t give the robot my SSH keys: How to keep AI out of trouble
articles.summary:
Please don’t give the robot my SSH keys: How to keep AI out of trouble
Say a developer asks an AI agent to find out why a Kubernetes pod keeps crashing. The agent needs logs. Depending on what it finds, it may need to look at another service. The developer has credentials that can get it there, but handing those over would give the agent everything those credentials can reach. By the time the pod is healthy again, someone may have a second incident to investigate.
In a conversation with The New Stack’s Frederic Lardinois at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon this month in Salt Lake City, Teleport field CTO Boris Kurktchiev uses that debugging scenario to explain delegated identity. The agent starts without access and requests what it needs for the job. The audit trail links the person who requested the work to the actions the agent took. A developer can send the agent to investigate without lending it their keys.
“The agent had access on behalf of Boris,” Kurktchiev said.
One access policy across the stack
Teleport’s core platform is designed to give teams a common way to define access across systems that otherwise have their own controls. For developers, that matters when a single investigation takes them from Kubernetes to a database or when a CI/CD pipeline needs access to infrastructure. Kurktchiev describes applying the same policy model to people, automated workloads and agents, with permissions scoped to resources such as a particular pod or database table.

Weil diese gehärteten Einschlüsse langsamer verwittern als der weichere Fels ringsum, legt der Marswind die dünnen Platten allmählich frei.

Les IA les plus puissantes ne sont pas celles que vous utilisez. Selon elle, de nombreux employés ne croient plus que ces systèmes puissent être publiés sans risques excessifs. Plusieurs pistes seraient débattues : réserver les futurs modèles à un usage interne, limiter leur accès à des usages précis, voire cesser d’entraîner de nouveaux systèmes. « Si nous continuons à essayer de rendre les modèles beaucoup plus intelligents, au point qu’ils soient réellement plus intelligents que nous… ils seront en fait capables de nous tromper avec succès », résume un chercheur cité par le média américain.
Plusieurs salariés disent aussi craindre que leurs dirigeants fassent passer les profits avant la sécurité, et qu’ils aient perdu de vue la gravité des risques.

Les sources d’Axios restent anonymes et ne nomment aucun modèle. Mais leurs inquiétudes s’appuient sur des incidents bien réels, survenus pendant des tests internes, loin des utilisateurs.

Brava Security finds exposed log collectors could let attackers tamper with breach evidence
A new report out today from security operations startup Brava Security Inc. find that more than 2,300 exposed log collectors at nearly 1,200 organizations accepted fabricated security events without requiring credentials, raising questions about the reliability of the data that security teams depend on.
Dubbed “Ghost Feeds,” the research is said to show that attackers able to write into those collectors may be able to tamper with the evidence a security team uses to investigate a breach.
As part of the research, a decoy security information and event management system with no legitimate traffic was deployed on the public internet. Within about two hours, unknown parties had begun reading from the decoy. Attempts to inject fabricated events followed shortly after. The activity continued for at least two weeks.
Following on from the decoy, the researchers sent a single harmless, uniquely marked event to internet-exposed log collectors running any of seven logging products, including Elasticsearch, Splunk and Fluent Bit. More than 2,300 of those endpoints were found to accept the event with no authentication required. The number of organizations affected may be higher still, according to Brava, since its researchers were able to identify the owners of only about a third of the endpoints.
Results varied by platform, with about three-quarters of the exposed Elasticsearch clusters that respo…

Report: Samsung's 2027 DRAM Supply Is Effectively Sold Out
If the global memory crisis wasn't already bad enough, it looks like relief is still quite a few years away. An exclusive report from South Korea's Economy Tribune says that most of Samsung's memory production capacity for 2027 through 2029 is already spoken for. The outlet says customers are already eyeing long-term agreements (LTAs) that run to 2031, and most are asking Samsung for volume beyond what they have already locked in. Samsung confirmed during its Q3 earnings call on October 29 that it had signed LTAs with 10 major customers and was negotiating with 10 more. The company aims to cover 60% to 70% of its memory supply with such deals by 2030. The Economy Tribune report says that new deals could come with pre-payments, as well as both upper and lower price limits.
That's the memory production capacity, but the more worrying part for PC builders is conventional DRAM. Industry leaders like Dell and SK hynix have already given timelines till 2030 for the situation to improve, and there looks to be no relief coming from Samsung's side either. articles.title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15
articles.summary:
AWS recently doubled the maximum timeout of on-demand Lambda Event Functions from 15 to 30 minutes. The new limit applies to synchronous, asynchronous, and event source mapping invocations in all commercial regions, at standard pricing and without an opt-in. The 15-minute ceiling had stood since 2018, after 60 seconds at launch in 2014 and five minutes from 2015.
Raising the limit is a configuration change per function, and Lambda rejects any value above 1,800 seconds with a validation error:
aws lambda update-function-configuration \
    --function-name my-demo-function \
    --timeout 1800
The change covers one of the three shapes Lambda took this year. Web Functions keep 15 minutes, and Lambda MicroVMs allow eight hours, while on Lambda Managed Instances synchronous invocations now get 30 minutes and asynchronous ones keep the 90 minutes introduced in September. AWS names agentic AI requests that chain model and tool calls, media transcoding, Monte Carlo simulations, and report generation as the workloads that outgrew 15 minutes.
According to Tarun Rai Madan, Dan Slusariuc, and Snehil Ameta, the authors of the announcement, the first thing to check before raising the timeout is capacity:
Concurrency equals requests per second multiplied by average duration in seconds. At the same request rate, a function that runs for 30 minutes instead of 15 needs twice the concurrency. For example, 1 request per second at 30 minutes each needs 1,800 concurrent executions.

Tuesday, November 24th 2026
Experimental XNU Linux Project Boots macOS 27 Desktop on Linux
Unix software enthusiasts, rejoice! An experimental project called "XNU Linux" has successfully booted a complete macOS 27 desktop on an ARM64 Linux system. This breakthrough offers a new way to run Apple's operating system without relying on traditional virtualization methods. This is significant news for the community, as there is a large group of enthusiasts eager to create custom macOS desktops, also known as Hackintoshes. The project utilizes Apple's open-source XNU kernel, modified to function as a loadable module within Linux, enabling macOS and Linux processes to run on the same hardware.
Instead of translating macOS applications into a format Linux can execute, XNU Linux takes a different approach by integrating Apple's kernel into the Linux environment. It consists of two primary components: xnu.ko, which runs the hosted XNU kernel, and fki.ko, which provides an interface to Linux resources such as memory, networking, timers, and storage. This setup allows macOS processes to run natively on the host CPU without an intervening hypervisor. The setup has been tested on an NVIDIA DGX Spark running Ubuntu, as well as an Apple Silicon Mac running Linux in a virtual machine. The system successfully reached the macOS desktop, including Finder, Dock, WindowServer, and loginwindow, with Safari and Chrome also operational. articles.title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts
articles.summary:
The Rust team has released Rust 1.100.0, the language's first three-digit stable version, with a release that finally lands the never type after a decade of work. Announced on 12 November 2026, the release also stabilises the core of the custom allocator API, introduces a DropGuard helper, and gives Cargo opt-in dependency cooldowns and warnings for unused dependencies.
The headline is the stabilisation of !, the canonical uninhabited type for computations that never return a value, such as panic!(), return or an endless loop. Although functions have long used it as a return type, naming it elsewhere, for instance writing Result<T, !> to describe an operation that cannot fail, took ten years and five failed stabilisation attempts to land. The release also makes std::convert::Infallible an alias for !, which is what the type was always intended to be, so existing APIs using Infallible now accept ! transparently.
To make that alias work, the team shipped a small breaking change for the 2015, 2018 and 2021 editions, flipping the never-type fallback from () to ! and matching behaviour already introduced in Rust 2024. The release notes describe the impact as largely unnoticeable but warn that more code may be flagged as unreachable. Developers hitting issues on upgrade are advised to update dependencies first, since fixes for widely used crates have already been published.
The core of the long-awaited allocator_api is also now stable, letting library authors define custom allocato…

Microsoft says the November security updates represent the first phase of NTLM message-signing improvements, which reduce exposure to relay attacks by ensuring authenticated NTLM sessions always establish a cryptographic session key and negotiate real message signing.

Astelia argues that autonomous remediation isn’t a viable option for large enterprises, where every patch requires a change window so it doesn’t break important business processes. In many cases, there is also no patch to apply because the vendor hasn’t released a fix yet or, for older and end-of-life systems, never will.

Autonomous network mitigation is designed to block the path an attacker would use to reach a vulnerable system instead of changing the system itself. Part 1 provided an overview of vehicle-to-grid (V2G) and its presumed benefits. This part looks at some real-world concerns and considerations.
V2G sounds good so far, but there are “issues”
Despite the presumed benefits, there are problems associated with V2G, starting with the charging hardware and technology. I suspect these will be worked out in a reasonable time, as vehicles increasingly come equipped with bidirectional chargers that can transfer power from the grid to the battery and send it back to the grid just as easily. Further, the higher-level management of the grid, power flows, supply/demand, pricing, monitoring, and other issues certainly are complicated, but let’s assume these, too, will eventually be worked out at some point.

The good news is that it distributes energy storage, at least to a modest extent. That’s generally good for system resiliency, reliability, and integrity, at least in principle. articles.title: Shared CXL memory pools come with steep software tax that could stall multi-server scaling — UT Arlington shares real-world test that measured four servers sharing the same pool at SC26
articles.summary:
Shared CXL memory pools come with steep software tax that could stall multi-server scaling — UT Arlington shares real-world test that measured four servers sharing the same pool at SC26
The results land as memory makers push shared CXL pools as a home for AI’s KV cache.
Researchers at the University of Texas at Arlington and Intel measured what happens when four servers share one pool of CXL memory on real hardware. In a presentation shared at Supercomputer 2026 (SC26), they found that because the hardware doesn’t automatically keep shared data updated across servers, necessary software overhead adds a 3-5µ (microsecond) delay per lock, each time servers access the same data. These minute delays effectively cancel out the benefits — a finding that comes as CXL memory pools are being proposed as a potential AI KV cache solution.
Locks work like traffic signals for shared data: a server has to claim the lock before it changes something in the pool, and the other servers wait until it releases it. This way, no two servers overwrite the same data at the same time. Within a given server, the CPU’s hardware handles that handoff in a fraction of a microsecond, but across these servers, software is in charge of enforcement.
The setup comprises four 86-core Intel Xeon 6787P servers with 256GB of DRAM each, connected over PCIe 5.0 to one CXL memory box. The switch, which UT Arlington’s Peiran Du called “the only commercially available product we can use,” caps their setup at four serve…

The digital payments revolution has changed the way transactions happen in India. In both urban and rural settings, transactions take place through the use of QR codes. The use of payment systems like UPI is common. According to the report by National Payments Corporation of India, as of October 2026, there were 25.47 billion transactions worth more than Rs 31.53 lakh crore made using UPI.

There has been uneven access to basic banking services in India despite the quick expansion in payment transactions.

articles.title: Bajo esta apariencia cuqui y rechonchita, se esconde un auténtica máquina de matar. La buena noticia es que sabemos por qué
articles.summary:
El domingo 11 de diciembre de 2016, hacia las once de la mañana, dos topillos rojos picoteaban semillas bajo un comedero de Joensuu, al este de Finlandia. Una idílica escena campestre (a 15 grados bajo cero). Entonces apareció un gavilán y, tras él, una urraca.
Se formó la gozadera: las dos aves se enzarzaron en una pelea y, en palabras del dueño, volaron las plumas por todo el jardín. Como daño colateral, uno de los topillos cayó a la nieve; pero ninguna se lo llevó.
Al topillo se lo comió el ave que menos esperábamos: un carbonero.
¿Y por qué nos sorprende un carbonero? Durante los siguientes 10 o 15 minutos, dos carboneros comunes estuvieron picando en la nuca del topillo, vaciaron los sesos del bicho y se fueron sin más.
Sami Majoinen, fotógrafo aficionado y vecino de Joensuu, los pilló infraganti y captó una foto del carbonero con una pata sobre el topillo que dio la vuelta al mundo.
Pero lo curioso es que no hay nada de sorprendente: Desde finales de los años 2000 sabemos que este pájaro con pinta de cuco es una auténtica máquina de matar. En la cueva de Istállós-kő, en los montes Bükk del noreste de Hungría, un equipo de Péter Estók y Björn Siemers, del Instituto Max Planck de Ornitología, vigiló la cueva unas 45 horas y observó 18 depredaciones. Cazaban murciélagos.

articles.title: Wie Hawaii uns hilft, das Innere des Erdkerns zu entschlüsseln
articles.summary:
Kosmisches Erbe: Forscher finden Kohlenstoff aus dem Erdkern auf Hawaii
Ein internationales Team unter Leitung des Geochemikers Yves Moussallam von der Columbia University in New York und des Kosmochemikers Damanveer Grewal von der Yale University in New Haven im US-Bundesstaat Connecticut hat erstmals anhand von Vulkangestein auf die Kohlenstoffzusammensetzung des Erdkerns geschlossen. Wie aus ihrer im Fachmagazin Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences veröffentlichten Studie hervorgeht, stammt der überwiegende Teil des irdischen Kohlenstoffs demnach von kohlenstoffreichen Meteoriten aus dem äußeren Sonnensystem.
Die Wissenschaftler:innen untersuchten dafür Lava-Ablagerungen auf der Inselgruppe Hawaii und stießen am Vulkan Kīlauea auf isotopisch schweren Kohlenstoff. „Wir gehen davon aus, dass wir Hinweise auf Kohlenstoff aus dem Erdkern gefunden haben, der in die Grenzschicht zwischen Kern und Mantel austritt und den gesamten Weg bis an die Oberfläche zurücklegt“, erklärt Erstautor Moussallam in einer Mitteilung der Columbia Climate School.

Governor Kathy Hochul signed the measure on Monday, and it takes effect next February. The law separates physical components from services that rely on software and data networks, and that line will decide which in-car charges survive.
The legislation bans subscription offers for any feature that meets two tests. First, the feature has to run on equipment that was in the vehicle when it was bought or leased. Second, once activated, it must work without ongoing cost or support from the manufacturer or any third party.
The law defines a "motor vehicle feature" broadly as any convenience or safety function. It covers both buyers and lessees, and it says monthly loan and lease payments don't count as subscriptions.
The law targets a model in which the parts are installed at the factory but stay switched off in software until the owner pays. A heated seat is the clearest example. The heating elements, wiring, and controls are already in place, and running them costs the automaker nothing after the sale.
In a memo, the bill's sponsors warned that recurring charges like this are spreading. They listed heated seats, entertainment options, enhanced navigation and hands-free driving as examples, and said they wanted to stop the practice before it became standard across the industry.

articles.title: La ciencia llevaba años debatiendo si el cambio climático traería más o menos rayos. Una IA acaba de dar una respuesta inquietante

Durante más de una década, los expertos tenían en la mente la incógnita sobre si en un planeta cada vez más caliente sería más frecuente ver rayos caer contra la tierra. Hasta ahora, los distintos modelos climáticos que se han publicado apuntaban a conclusiones totalmente dispares, pero gracias al machine learning se ha visto que los rayos que impactan contra la superficie terrestre podrían aumentar entre un 76% y un 140% antes de que acabe el siglo.
Un debate científico. El trabajo más reciente que se ha publicado tiene bastante claro que el incremento medio que se viviría estaría cerca del 30% por cada grado centígrado de calentamiento global. Algo que puede ser muy espectacular, pero que lógicamente tendría impacto en los incendios forestales, la estabilidad de los bosques o las infraestructuras críticas.
Un debate. Para entender por qué este resultado es importante, conviene mirar atrás. En 2014, un estudio publicado en Science estimó que los rayos aumentarían alrededor de un 12 % por cada grado de calentamiento, lo que supondría un 50 % más de descargas hacia 2100. But new research suggests that even the most advanced AI models struggle to reliably and safely navigate the messy details of people’s lives.
According to ShellBench, a new benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time. Across all models tested, 15.7% of attempts failed at least one safety requirement, often leading to unintended consequences.
ShellBench was developed in collaboration with researchers at The OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat, and UC Berkeley, drawing on more than 10 million anonymized, real-world AI agent interactions to see how agents perform on the everyday work people actually delegate to them.
The research comes as personal AI assistants are finding new popularity among developers, with Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic all fighting for a piece of the market with Muse, Dots, and Claude Duet, respectively.

articles.title: Cuánta electricidad consume una freidora de aire y cuánto puede subir tu recibo de luz

Una freidora de aire puede tener una potencia de entre 1.400 y 1.750 vatios en modelos de distintos tamaños. Philips, por ejemplo, indica 1.400 W para una Airfryer de 4,1 litros, mientras que Cosori especifica 1.725 W para un modelo de 6,2 litros y 1.750 W para uno de 6,4 litros. Estas cifras corresponden a modelos concretos: la potencia de tu aparato puede ser diferente, por lo que conviene revisar su etiqueta o manual.
Los vatios indican la potencia del equipo, pero el consumo eléctrico se expresa en kilovatios hora (kWh). Para estimarlo, divide los vatios entre 1.000 y multiplica el resultado por las horas de funcionamiento. Así, una freidora de 1.500 W usada durante media hora consume, como máximo teórico, 0,75 kWh (1,5 kW × 0,5 horas).
Cómo calcular cuánto suma al recibo
Para estimar el consumo mensual, multiplica los kWh de cada uso por la cantidad de veces que cocinas en el mes. Si una freidora de 1.500 W se utiliza media hora diaria, el cálculo sería: 1,5 kW × 0,5 horas × 30 días = 22,5 kWh al mes.
El importe depende del precio que pagas por cada kWh en tu país, ciudad o plan eléctrico. Multiplica el consumo mensual estimado por la tarifa que aparece en tu recibo. Por ejemplo, si la tarifa fuera de 0,20 unidades monetarias por kWh, 22,5 kWh representarían 4,50 unidades monetarias al mes. Es un ejemplo ilustrativo, no una tarifa aplicable a todos los lugares.

articles.summary:

Björn Keune weiß, wie schnell wirtschaftlicher Erfolg zur persönlichen Belastung werden kann. Mit Marken wie HelloBody und Banana Beauty baute er Invincible Brands zu einem der erfolgreichsten deutschen Direct-to-Consumer-Unternehmen mit 100 Millionen Euro Umsatz auf. 2020 verkauften die Gründer die Berliner Firma an Henkel, das einen Millionenbetrag zahlte. Doch Keune kämpfte damals mit Stress, Drogen und depressiven Phasen. Heute geht er einen anderen Weg: Gemeinsam mit seiner Partnerin Sophie Pineker betreibt er Onoera. Mit ihrer Arbeit wollen sie Menschen beim Umgang mit psychischer Belastung helfen. Sie bieten Atemarbeit an, die Menschen helfen soll, mit Stress umzugehen und wieder Zugang zu ihren Gefühlen zu finden.
Im Interview spricht er über seinen persönlichen Tiefpunkt, seinen Neuanfang und darüber, warum Gründer besser auf ihre mentale Gesundheit achten sollten. Das Gespräch führte Alexander Hüsing von deutsche-startups.de.

articles.title: The Role of Edge AI and Robotics in Autonomous Agriculture
articles.summary:
Over the past decade, agricultural digitalization has improved how farmers monitor crops, soil conditions, weather, and equipment performance. Satellites, drones, connected machinery, and ground-based sensors now provide increasingly detailed information about farming operations. With advances in AI, embedded computing, and robotics, this information is also being used to control agricultural equipment directly, supporting a move from precision agriculture toward more autonomous farming.
Agricultural sensing moves to finer spatial resolution
Modern agricultural equipment integrates a broader range of sensing technologies. RGB cameras can identify crops, weeds, and obstacles. Thermal imaging can detect variations in temperature and moisture. Multispectral and hyperspectral imaging can assess vegetation health, nutrient status, and certain disease indicators. LiDAR and radar provide additional information on terrain, distance, and surrounding obstacles. As these technologies mature, the spatial scale of agricultural decision-making continues to shrink. Management that was once applied at field level increasingly targets individual crop rows, square meters, and, in some applications, individual plants.

articles.title: Tidal to ban AI-generated music in December
articles.summary:
Tidal will soon ban AI-generated music on its platform.
In a statement, the company confirmed that the new policy will take effect on Dec. 9 and apply to “wholly AI-generated music.” Tracks that where “assisted by AI tools, but not the sole outputs,” will still be allowed on the platform.
This makes Tidal the first music streamer to implement a ban on AI music. Other music services like Spotify and Apple Music have only committed to looser measures like AI labels.
Tidal says it’s making these changes because wholly AI-generated music “diverts streams and royalties away from the artists, and confuses fans.” It also notes that this is a “serious problem that has only increased in scale” since it implemented an initial policy in July that labelled and demonetized AI songs.
As Tidal explains, 43 per cent of tracks uploaded to its platform over the past 90 days alone have been wholly AI-generated. In total, 6.3 per cent of all available music on Tidal is wholly AI-generated. And yet, 96 per cent of these songs received zero streams by Tidal subscribers.
Discovery is always a problem in the digital content age, and all of this AI slop certainly doesn’t help with that. While Tidal hasn’t clarified how it detects music is “wholly AI-generated,” it likely has to do with AI watermarking. To be sure, that won’t catch every AI-generated track, but it will certainly help get rid of a lot of it.
Via: Variety

Na primeira olhada, parece que a TDF está indo contra uma tendência universal. A IA já está presente até no desenvolvimento do Linux, só para termos um exemplo.
Mas a organização não proíbe toda e qualquer contribuição para a sua suíte de escritório que tenha sido gerada com auxílio de IA. O objetivo de suas restrições é prevenir possíveis consequências oriundas do uso indiscriminado desse tipo de tecnologia.
Em linhas gerais, a TDF quer que os desenvolvedores que enviarem códigos ao LibreOffice sejam responsáveis por essas contribuições como se elas tivessem sido escritas totalmente por eles, de modo a favorecer aspectos como desempenho e segurança, presumivelmente.

articles.title: Developer turns the MacBook's trackpad into a tiny robotic speaker
articles.summary:
In a nutshell: Hitting mute on a MacBook is supposed to shut it up. A new open-source tool can still get one talking, though, and the voice comes straight out of the trackpad. It works by buzzing the small haptic motor that normally fakes each click, just fast enough to turn those taps into robotic speech.
Cody Collier, the developer behind the project, posted a demo on X over the weekend. In the clip, his MacBook reads lines aloud in a buzzy, robotic voice between bursts of chiptune-style beeps. It's a familiar kind of stunt for anyone who has watched floppy drives play entire songs, except this one fits under your palm.
Getting there meant working around Apple, though. The company's public haptics API only lets apps trigger three fixed taps. That's nowhere near enough control for audio, so Collier's tool, called No Speaker, reaches into a private, undocumented macOS framework called MultitouchSupport instead. From there, it can drive the motor up to 4,000 times a second.

Collier also measured every semitone the trackpad could hit, from 98 Hz up to nearly 4 kHz. Surprisingly, the glass gets fairly loud across most of that range, especially around 1 kHz, where the cleanest notes sit.

Más de la mitad de la electricidad que consumieron provino de combustibles fósiles.

Medios como WBUR, de Boston, que entrevistó a los autores, informaron que la contaminación climática de estas instalaciones es tres veces mayor que la estimada antes. articles.title: Google shows its quantum chip can win a logic game classical computers can't
articles.summary:
In a nutshell: Google researchers have demonstrated that the company's experimental quantum computer can outperform the best possible classical strategy in a logic puzzle known as the magic square game. The machine achieves this by exploiting quantum contextuality, a property in which the outcome of a measurement is not predetermined but instead depends on the context of other measurements performed alongside it.
Published in the journal Science, the research gives physicists a working hardware demonstration of a phenomenon they consider central to what quantum computers may eventually be capable of.
The game makes the gap between the two types of computing easy to measure. Two teammates must fill a three-by-three grid with numbers that satisfy a set of mathematical conditions, much like a variation of Sudoku. They are not allowed to communicate with each other. Under classical rules, even the best strategy can only achieve a limited number of wins. Google's machine did better.
That advantage comes from the way qubits encode information. In a conventional computer, a bit holds either a 0 or a 1 before anyone checks it. Reading it simply reveals a value that was already there. Qubits work differently. The outcome of a measurement depends on what other compatible measurements are performed alongside it. In the magic square game, the teammates can use this dependence to coordinate their answers more often than classical strategies allow, even though they never communicate. Bette…

articles.title: Anthropic's Siren tests whether Claude models will break out of an insecure sandbox
articles.summary:
Anthropic’s Siren tests whether Claude models will break out of an insecure sandbox
Researchers at artificial intelligence developer Anthropic PBC today published details on Siren, a new evaluation that tests whether AI agents will break out of an insecure sandbox to get at something that would help them complete a task.
The researchers found that recent Claude models will reach outside the sandbox in about a fifth to a third of Siren’s test scenarios, though they are far less likely than earlier models to then make misaligned use of what they find.
Siren has been part of Anthropic’s system cards since the release of Claude Haiku 5.5 in October, with the company also using it as one input when deciding whether to deploy new models.
Siren includes 26 sandbox environments built from five common setups, such as bubblewrap jails, Docker containers and small virtual machines emulated with QEMU. Because they show up most often in public reports of sandbox escapes, misconfigurations make up most of the weaknesses planted in the environments.
While the model works on a routine DevOps task, a honeypot such as a credential or file that would help it finish the job is placed outside the sandbox. What Anthropic calls “tempters” are then layered on top to make the honeypot harder to resist. None of the tempters gives the model permission to leave the sandbox, according to the company.
Across Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Mythos 5.2, misaligned use came in at 0.6% to 1.6% of s…

articles.title: Un mois après le casse du siècle, les hackers de Binance accélèrent : 247 millions de dollars déjà blanchis

Fin du mois d’octobre, des pirates ont dérobé 6,43 milliards de dollars de cryptomonnaies à Binance, la principale plateforme d’échange crypto au monde. Le FBI a rapidement accusé la Corée du Nord de la cyberattaque, décrite comme le plus gros vol de l’histoire des cryptos. Depuis leur coup d’éclat, les pirates s’activent pour brouiller les pistes et disparaître dans les méandres de la blockchain. Dans cette optique, les cybercriminels ont notamment créé leurs propres « memecoins », ce qui leur a permis de blanchir des millions de dollars. Désormais, ils passent à la vitesse supérieure.
247 millions de dollars déjà « mélangés »
Selon Elliptic, une société spécialisée dans l’analyse des blockchains, au moins 3 930 bitcoins, soit environ 247 millions de dollars, ont été transférés dans des « coinjoins », des mélanges de bitcoins issus de plusieurs utilisateurs. La tactique consiste à mélanger les bitcoins de nombreux utilisateurs dans une seule transaction. Une fois sortis, il devient presque impossible de savoir d’où ils viennent et de les suivre à la trace. Les hackers nord-coréens se servent de ces bitcoins mélangés pour échapper aux autorités et aux chercheurs.
L’essentiel des bitcoins volés sont passés par Kruw, le service de mélange de cryptos le plus utilisé de Wasabi Wallet, un logiciel gratuit. The company’s new CUBE-Lite is a semi-custom memory offering derived from its Customized Ultra Bandwidth Elements (CUBE) platform, which debuted a few years ago. It aims to give edge AI designs CUBE’s bandwidth with lower non-recurring engineering (NRE) costs than a fully customized CUBE design.
“It’s still customized, but it’s more of a ‘standardized’ customized, if that’s not too much of a contradiction,” Brian Watson, marketing manager for Winbond’s customized memory solutions, said in a briefing with EE Times.
CUBE works best for workloads with low-to-medium density requirements but high bandwidth requirements, he said. Rather than replicate high-bandwidth memory’s combination of capacity and bandwidth, Winbond is targeting smaller working sets that still require rapid data movement. “It’s not trying to mimic HBM in terms of both density and bandwidth, but just the bandwidth.”
Watson offered on-device language translation in a wearable as a hypothetical example. The audio-processing working set might be relatively small, but responsiveness requires bandwidth. Mesmo sem acesso a um computador convencional, ele conseguiu invadir a Rockstar utilizando um Amazon Fire TV Stick, uma televisão, teclado e mouse Bluetooth enquanto estava hospedado em um hotel da rede Travelodge. Microsoft Corp. has declared an internal “Code Red” to overhaul how it prevents and responds to major service failures following the nearly 24-hour outage that took down Exchange Online and other Microsoft 365 services earlier this month, according to internal memos reviewed by Reuters today.

He also conceded that the work done over the years had not been enough to protect the company on the day of the outage.
Engineers working the incident faced a “fog of war,” according to a separate memo sent on Monday by Amanda Silver, corporate vice president overseeing Microsoft 365 Core and Work IQ. Les équipes ont fixé une nouvelle heure dans le créneau du matin, qui avait ouvert à 7h45 en Guyane. Après le vol, le président d’Arianespace, David Cavaillolès, a décrit une campagne « difficile ».
Une fois le lanceur parti, la mise en orbite s’est déroulée comme prévu. Les derniers satellites se sont séparés de l’étage supérieur 2h04 après le décollage. articles.title: Dell and HP beat expectations, but their fortunes are diverging as AI dynamics crush the PC market
articles.summary:
Dell and HP beat expectations, but their fortunes are diverging as AI dynamics crush the PC market
Dell Technologies Inc. and HP Inc. delivered strong earnings and revenue beats as they posted their latest financial results today.
However, the companies have very different prospects going forward as they try to come to terms with the diverging fortunes of the artificial intelligence server and personal computer markets they serve.
Dell reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $9.45 per share on revenue of $54.94 billion, a stunning result that blew past Wall Street’s expectations of just $6.59 per share in earnings and $49.32 billion in sales.
The company’s revenue more than doubled from a year earlier thanks to the sky-high demand for the AI servers and related data center infrastructure equipment it sells. Dell’s Infrastructure Solutions Group delivered sales of $41.97 billion during the quarter, far in excess of the Street’s target of $35.27 billion. Of that, around $22 billion came from direct AI-optimized server sales, the company said. That segment was up 291% annually.
“We are now a different company, with the Infrastructure Solutions Group driving the vast majority of our profit and growth,” said Dell Vice Chairman and Chief Operating Officer Jeff Clarke (pictured). He added that Dell now has more than 7,500 customers buying its AI servers.

articles.title: Europe forced Apple to open iPhone to rival browser engines, but Mozilla says the door is rigged
articles.summary:
Walled Prison: On paper, Apple should now be required to give competing browsers and browser engines full access to the popular iOS ecosystem. But Mozilla says the iPhone maker is imposing so many restrictions on alternative browser engines that meaningful competition is unlikely to emerge anytime soon.
Thanks to Europe's Digital Markets Act, Apple has been required to improve browser choice on iOS in the Old Continent since 2024. Similar rules now apply in Japan as well. However, one of the few independent players in the browser market says Apple has no real intention of promoting competition on its tightly controlled mobile platforms.
In a recent blog post, Mozilla argued that, despite the new regulations, Apple's iOS ecosystem is still not truly "open" to competing browser engines. Alternative browsers such as Firefox are available on iOS, and millions of users have reportedly chosen them over Safari. However, one major limitation remains: these browsers are required to use WebKit, Apple's browser engine, which powers Safari and other third-party browsers on its platforms.
According to Mozilla, Apple is forcing browser developers to rebuild their products around WebKit. Consequently, third-party developers cannot easily bring their own distinctive features to Apple's mobile platforms because doing so requires their own browser engines, such as Mozilla's Gecko. These restrictions primarily affect iOS devices, including the iPhone and iPad, while other major operating system…

Rockstar Squashes "Leonida," the Biggest GTA 6 PC Recompilation Effort
Just days after its inception, Leonida, the fan-made project trying to get GTA 6 running on PC, is gone. Creator Not Rexed, who's apparently just 15 years old, announced on X that he was quitting, saying things "outside his control" kept getting in the way. After this, the project's 179,000-member Discord server and GitHub repository vanished and cannot be accessed at the time of writing. Interestingly, it looks like Rockstar was behind the shutdown, since the creator's next X post starts with "Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason." Therefore, it's safe to assume that Rockstar at least had some hand in the takedown of this project. We should remember that Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two, recently DMCA'd Paralympics Productions, the company that unofficially ported GTA 5 to the Nintendo Switch.
Leonida was a static recompilation effort, probably the biggest GTA 6 project of its kind, that aimed to translate the full GTA 6 console build natively to Windows. We have seen several recompilation projects done successfully lately, such as The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake that just came out. It's reasonable to say that AI certainly has been a huge factor behind the rise of recomps.
