Epochal launches with $100M to help developers train predictive AI models
Artificial intelligence tooling startup Epochal AI Inc. launched today with $100 million in funding.
The capital was provided by Chief Executive Officer Guodong Zhang, a machine learning researcher who earlier co-founded xAI Corp. He established Epochal earlier this year with two other xAI co-founders, Zihang Dai and Manuel Kroiss. Ahora hay doce tumbas, una posible inscripción en latín y un debate muy gallego: qué hacer con los muertos que aparecen donde nadie se los espera.
Qué hay debajo. La excavación de urgencia, entre el 22 de septiembre y el 15 de octubre, documentó doce sepulturas en 260 metros cuadrados, fechadas entre finales del siglo XII y principios del XIII. Ocho están delimitadas por lajas, una tiene cubierta y tres son fosas simples. Todas miran de este a oeste, como manda el rito cristiano.
Con la iglesia hemos topado. En la cimentación del ábside de la iglesia actual (de 1854), apareció una posible lauda que alude, presuntamente, a la fórmula latina “Post Mortem Christi”. Documentos de los años 998 y 1199 ya citan una iglesia de Santa Baia, lo que refuerza que hubo un templo románico anterior. También salieron 1.236 restos óseos del cementerio más reciente, de al menos 25 personas, ahora en una fosa común parroquial. Es el primer yacimiento arqueológico identificado en casco urbano.

Employees working at frontier artificial intelligence model companies Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC have been butting heads with executives over advanced models whose reasoning is such that the models pose to danger to humanity, according to a report by Axios today based on more than two dozen sources familiar with the current standoff at the companies.

It appears that some staff err on the side of caution and believe the training should stop completely while others believe they can be reined in.
“If we continue trying to make models much smarter, such that they’re actually smarter than us… they will in fact be able to trick us successfully,” one of the researchers told Axios. “And once you get to that point, many of the schemes that we’ve had at work up until now sort of go out the window.”

En la agricultura hay problemas que se resuelven con maquinaria de última generación, otros con productos químicos y algunos con una buena dosis de imaginación. En Uruguay, un productor de limones ecológicos acabó desarrollando un insólito invento después de descubrir que sus mejores aliadas contra las malas hierbas tenían un pequeño defecto: un apetito descomunal.
Todo empezó en 2019. Martín Guarini, un agricultor de Araminda, en el departamento uruguayo de Canelones, había decidido reconvertir su explotación de limoneros a la producción ecológica. Pronto se encontró con un problema: eliminar las malas hierbas sin recurrir a los herbicidas convencionales resultaba caro y laborioso.
Probó con maquinaria y preparados ecológicos a base de vinagre, pero ninguna alternativa le convenció. Fue entonces cuando pensó en recurrir a una tecnología que llevaba miles de años funcionando: las ovejas.
Los cortacéspedes tenían un defecto. Durante los primeros días, el experimento parecía un éxito. Los animales eliminaban la vegetación sobrante, fertilizaban el suelo con sus excrementos y abrían una nueva vía de ingresos mediante la producción ganadera.
Sin embargo, las ovejas pronto descubrieron que las ramas inferiores de los limoneros jóvenes también eran comestibles, provocando daños considerables en los árboles. Guarini tenía el cortacésped perfecto, pero necesitaba instalarle una especie de limitador de altura.

articles.title: Ladybird é um navegador feito do zero para desafiar o Chrome

Ladybird é um navegador feito do zero para desafiar o Chrome
Ao contrário da maioria dos navegadores atuais, o Ladybird não é baseado no Chromium e conta com um motor próprio.
Parece até lei: todo novo projeto de navegador que surgiu nos últimos anos tem como base o Chromium e, por conta disso, renderiza páginas por meio do motor Blink. Mas o Ladybird é diferente. Esse é o nome de um browser que está sendo desenvolvido do zero e que, portanto, tem um motor próprio.
Entenda, como motor, o mecanismo que permite ao navegador interpretar o código de uma página web e, então, apresentar um conteúdo visual e interativo para o usuário.
Mas é extremamente difícil desenvolver um motor, ainda mais com uma web tão cheia de recursos como a que temos hoje. Isso explica, pelo menos em parte, o fato de, além do próprio Google Chrome, browsers como Edge, Opera, Vivaldi e Brave seguirem a base do projeto Chromium, com motor Blink.
O Firefox é uma exceção, pois conta com um motor próprio, o Gecko — exceto o Firefox para iOS, por “culpa” da Apple. Falando em Apple, o Safari também é uma exceção, pois tem o motor WebKit como base. O Ladybird chega para ser uma quarta opção nesse cenário.
O Ladybird surge como um projeto independente, sob liderança de Andreas Kling. O desenvolvedor é mais conhecido por ter criado o sistema operacional aberto SerenityOS, projeto que ele deixou de liderar em 2024 justamente para se dedicar ao navegador.

Rajiv Ramaswami to step down as Nutanix begins hunt for its next CEO
Rajiv Ramaswami is stepping down from his role as chief executive of Nutanix Inc., six years after he joined the hyperconverged cloud infrastructure company from its rival VMware Inc.
In a letter to company employees, Ramaswami (pictured) said he’s going to continue in the role for the time being while he works with Nutanix’s board of directors to identify a successor and assist with the transition. “After that, I will continue to serve as a senior advisor to the company for a period of time,” he said in the letter.
Ramaswami, who is 60 years old, did not give any reason for his coming departure, but the letter seems to indicate that he’s not ready to retire just yet.

articles.title: Du jamais-vu depuis 2013 : voici Ladybird, le navigateur qui ne dépend pas de Google, Apple ou Mozilla

Le canal est désormais continu, mis à jour automatiquement, et l’avertissement ne cache rien : « C’est une alpha, certains sites ne fonctionneront pas et il plantera parfois ».
Un web à trois moteurs, tous branchés sur la publicité
Chrome, Edge, Opera et consorts reposent sur Blink, Safari sur WebKit, Firefox sur Gecko. Le dernier moteur indépendant à avoir pesé s’est éteint en 2013, quand Opera a abandonné son Presto pour rejoindre la base de Chrome, un chemin que Microsoft a suivi en 2020 avec Edge.
Les trois moteurs sont open source. Blink et WebKit appartiennent pourtant à des géants de la publicité et du matériel, et l’essentiel des revenus de Mozilla provient d’un accord de recherche signé avec Google. « Ils sont tous financés par l’empire publicitaire de Google », résumait dès 2024 Chris Wanstrath, le cofondateur de GitHub qui a doté le projet d’un million de dollars. Ces mêmes acteurs siègent d’ailleurs aux consortiums qui écrivent les standards du web.
Ladybird, lancé en 2022 dans le sillage du système expérimental SerenityOS, n’emprunte pas une ligne de code à Blink, WebKit ou Gecko. Andreas Kling, son fondateur, est un ancien développeur WebKit passé par Apple et Nokia. articles.title: “Automatizar toda la investigación en IA”: el escenario que describe el jefe de IA de Meta, Alexandr Wang

Alexandr Wang, director de Inteligencia Artificial de Meta y responsable de sus Laboratorios de Superinteligencia, encendió el debate tecnológico este fin de semana al publicar en X que “la superinteligencia está llegando”. Según Wang, los modelos de IA alcanzarán pronto un nivel suficiente para automatizar toda la investigación en el campo.
La declaración llegó en un momento particular: un fin de semana en el que la burbuja de la inteligencia artificial pareció desinflarse, justo antes de recomponerse de forma controvertida.
Wang no mencionó ni la salida a bolsa de Anthropic ni la dimisión y posterior reincorporación de Jensen Huang en Nvidia. Su atención estaba puesta en otro hito que, a su juicio, cambia las reglas del juego.
Qué significa automatizar la investigación en inteligencia artificial
Automatizar toda la investigación en IA implica que los propios sistemas de inteligencia artificial pasarían a diseñar, probar y mejorar nuevos modelos sin depender del trabajo humano en esas etapas. Es el escenario que Wang describió como inminente, al sostener que los modelos “serán claramente lo suficientemente inteligentes” para asumir esa tarea por completo.
Para Wang, los obstáculos que faltan superar ya no tienen que ver con la capacidad intelectual de los sistemas. Escribió que lo que resta resolver “ya no es la inteligencia, sino el conocimiento especializado, la infraestructura y la experimentación”. articles.title: Formal verification startup Sequent raises $2.2M to prove code obeys its safety rules
articles.summary:
Formal verification startup Sequent raises $2.2M to prove code obeys its safety rules
Formal verification startup Sequent Inc. today announced that it has raised $2.2 million in new funding to take its Alan proof platform out of early access.
Founded in London in January, Sequent offers a platform that uses artificial intelligence to find mathematical proofs that code obeys the safety rules its engineers set. Decentralized exchange Curve Finance is its first paying customer.
Curve also figures in how Sequent got started. Chief Executive Charles Cooper, who leads development of Vyper, one of the two main programming languages for Ethereum, inadvertently introduced a flaw into the Vyper compiler in 2021. Though the bug was fixed within months, programs already running on the blockchain could not be updated, leaving older Curve pools and other projects exposed when attackers used the flaw to take more than $50 million in July 2023.
Following the incident, Ramana Kumar, now Sequent’s chief technology officer and formerly an AI safety researcher at Google DeepMind, offered to help prove the Vyper compiler correct. Kumar co-created CakeML, a compiler proved correct all the way down to the instructions a computer runs.
Cooper believes the lesson reaches far beyond crypto, saying that “smart contracts taught us that anything that can be exploited will be.” Banks, governments and companies running older systems have relied on keeping their code private, according to Cooper, who said A…

Et pour cause, ces morceaux ne sont pas le fruit de créations humaines, mais d’intelligences artificielles. Il faut dire qu’avec la progression fulgurante de l’IA notamment en ce qui concerne la génération de musique, la tentation de faire fortune en diffusant des morceaux générés par IA sur les plates-formes de streaming est très tentante. El Narrador abre entonces una ventana que no se ve en pantalla. Con la tecla de mayúsculas fijas apretada y las flechas, el atacante llega a un enlace de configuración, abre los Ajustes de Windows y, desde ahí, activa la reproducción automática de unidades externas. articles.title: Avec le tout nouveau Claude Ship, l'IA d'Anthropic ne se contente plus d'écrire du code, elle le valide
articles.summary:
Anthropic a lancé Claude Ship cette semaine, un service capable de relire, corriger et approuver les pull requests des développeurs. Réservé aux offres professionnelles et à GitHub, il laisse aux équipes le dernier mot sur ce que l'IA peut valider seule.
L'entreprise Anthropic a lancé Claude Ship le lundi 23 novembre, qui se présente comme un ensemble d'outils d'intelligence artificielle qui prend en charge les pull requests, ces demandes de modification soumises avant d'intégrer du code à un projet. Le service relit chaque modification, corrige les problèmes signalés, puis décide si elle peut être fusionnée, selon des règles fixées par chaque équipe. Une nouvelle commande, /ship, permet aussi aux développeurs de l'utiliser directement depuis Claude Code.
Claude Ship, ou l'art de ne plus courir après les relecteurs
Quiconque a déjà ouvert une pull request connaît la routine. On attaque la tâche suivante, puis les remarques arrivent. On replonge dans un code qu'on croyait derrière soi, on corrige, on attend une nouvelle relecture. Il reste ensuite à trouver le collègue qui voudra bien valider. Exiger un humain pour chaque modification reste tenable tant que des humains écrivent chaque ligne. Mais chez Anthropic, c'est désormais Claude qui écrit l'essentiel du code de l'équipe Claude Code, et l'entreprise voulait que tout ce qui suit la pull request avance au même rythme.

articles.title: OpenAI and Cisco Unveil AI-Assisted Linux Security Tool to Block Exploits Before Patching
articles.summary:
OpenAI and Cisco have teamed up to launch Shirudo (meaning "shield" in Japanese), an open-source Linux runtime that allows artificial intelligence (AI) agents to defend systems without downtime.
"It lets agents write dynamic eBPF controls to shield systems from exploits, giving defenders more time to test and roll out patches," OpenAI said in a post on X.
The AI upstart called the initiative a "first step" toward "self-defending infrastructure" that can adapt itself to new threats while the services continue to run and enable defenders to test and deploy fixes without any disruption.
The development comes as AI is accelerating vulnerability discovery, finding critical bugs in foundational software used to power internet-connected software.
Shirudo is being pitched as a way for defenders to test temporary safeguards (aka shields) and check if they block behavior that exposes a vulnerability, while letting legitimate requests pass through. Once a shield is approved by an operator, it can be deployed without having to stop the service.
The idea is to avoid a complete service disruption to block a line of attack simply because both an exploit and a legitimate request may rely on the same underlying Linux operation.
To achieve this, Shirudo makes use of eBPF (short for extended Berkeley Packet Filter), a technology that makes it possible to run lightweight, sandboxed programs inside the kernel without the need for modifying the system code or restarting it.

articles.title: 3D printer tool changers are cheaper than ever, now starting at just $599 with multiple models at lowest-ever pricing — these game-changing multi-material, multi-color, filament-saving printers are all on sale
articles.summary:
3D printer tool changers are cheaper than ever, now starting at just $599 with multiple models at lowest-ever pricing — these game-changing multi-material, multi-color, filament-saving printers are all on sale
Say hello to a new 3D printer and goodbye to wasteful filament “poop.”
Tool changers — 3D printers with multiple heads — have been a major focus of the industry for more than a year, and for good reason. Multiple heads mean you don’t have to purge the nozzle every time your print swaps colors or materials, which has the dual benefit of making complex prints much faster while saving a massive amount of filament waste or “poop,” which is a problem with more traditional multi-color AMS, single-toolhead printers.
But while these tool changers typically cost multiple thousands of dollars a few years ago, they’ve gotten much more affordable in the past year, starting with Snapmaker’s sub-$1,000 U1 (now just $699) and then Fashforge’s Creator 5 not long after. And both of those printers, plus a traditional four-color AMS printer designed to minimize wasted filament, are all on sale at their lowest-ever prices as we head into Black Friday.
So if you’re thinking of diving into the 3D printing realm or your existing printer is getting long in the tooth, now is a great time to make the leap to a tool changer and see how it can change your printing game — or perhaps your printing business.

articles.title: WHMCS SQL Injection Could Expose Customer Data and Admin Password Hashes without Login
articles.summary:
A flaw in WHMCS's shopping cart, the billing and automation platform many web hosting companies use to run their businesses, could allow anyone on the internet to retrieve customer records and administrator password hashes from an installation's database. No login is needed.
The company disclosed the SQL injection yesterday along with two other flaws that need a logged-in client, and released fixed versions. It has not reported attacks using any of the three.
Because no login is needed, the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-82981 (CVSS score: 8.7), is within reach of anyone who can load the shopping cart of a vulnerable installation over the internet.
The records an attacker could pull include clients' personal and support information as well as admin accounts with their hashed passwords, according to the company's advisory. A stolen hash is not a working password, but it gives attackers something to try to crack offline.
The 9.0.10 and 8.13.8 updates shipped yesterday, and the release notes list them as maintenance releases. For the 9.1 series, the security advisory names 9.1.2 as the fix, but that build had not yet appeared on the company's 9.1 release notes page at publication time.
Fixes are available only for supported versions, so installations on the 8.0 to 8.12 series must upgrade to a fixed release.
Installing the updates falls to self-hosted administrators, since WHMCS Cloud installations are updated automatically, according to the company's updating documentation.

articles.title: Google Researcher Shows How a Single Bit Change in .NET Files Bypassed Windows Code Integrity
articles.summary:
A quirk in how the .NET Framework loads a program file let a local attacker run untrusted code past two separate protections on Windows built to block it, Google Project Zero researcher James Forshaw showed in a write-up published yesterday.
The same loading behavior bypassed Oracle VirtualBox's process hardening on Windows hosts, tracked as CVE-2026-87268, and Windows code integrity, tracked as CVE-2026-108398.
Oracle fixed the VirtualBox flaw in September, and Microsoft fixed the Windows one on October 13, both before the write-up appeared.
VirtualBox on Windows monitors the system calls that load program files into its virtual machine processes, so a less-trusted user on the same computer cannot push code into them. Forshaw got past that watch through the .NET Framework.
The framework can run a .NET program file from a plain copy in memory when the normal way of loading it, as an executable image, fails. Version 4 of the framework takes that fallback on one specific error, and the memory copy skips the image checks a loaded program would face.
The VirtualBox check returned that error for any .NET file compiled as AnyCPU, a form meant to run on any processor, so an unchanged file loaded through the path the hardening never inspects.
To get the file loaded while a virtual machine was started, he registered a COM object in the current user's settings that a protected VirtualBox process would pull in, a method known as COM hijacking. He set out the mechanism in his technical a…

articles.title: Hackers Found a Way Around GitHub SHA Pinning. This Webinar Explains How to Close the Gap
articles.summary:
Pinning GitHub Actions to an exact version of their code, known as SHA pinning, has become the go-to defense against software supply chain attacks. Attackers have already found a way around it.
In March 2026, the hackers who hijacked Trivy, a widely used open-source security scanner, planted malicious code that looked like it came from GitHub's official checkout tool. They even labeled it a security fix. Teams pinned to it would have passed every check.
The trick works because GitHub lets copies of a project, called forks, share code with the original. In May, the same technique hit the popular actions-cool/issues-helper tool, stealing credentials from the pipelines that ran it.
The lesson: pinning guarantees the code won't change, but not who wrote it.
That gap is the focus of an upcoming webinar, GitHub Actions Security Beyond SHA Pinning. If your team treats pinning as the finish line, save your seat to learn what it actually protects you from, and what it doesn't.
Immutability Is Not Provenance
Pinning earned its reputation. When the tj-actions/changed-files compromise repointed tags to a malicious commit across more than 23,000 repositories in March 2025, teams that had pinned to SHAs were unaffected.
GitHub now lets administrators enforce pinning as an organization-wide policy, and few security teams argue against it.

articles.title: Iran-Aligned Volant Manticore Uses IPFS-Based KuboShell Backdoor in Espionage Campaigns

A previously undocumented Iran-aligned cyber espionage group called Volant Manticore has targeted telecommunications companies, airlines, and critical infrastructure in Cyprus.
Central to the group's operations is a backdoor called KuboShell that uses the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) for command-and-control (C2) and deploys Homa, a post-compromise framework that's a reimplementation of MuddyWater's MuddyC2Go. Evidence indicates that the threat actor has been operational since late August 2025.
Also delivered alongside these tools are Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) programs like MeshCentral and NetLock RMM. In tandem, the group has been observed orchestrating credential harvesting campaigns to collect email and corporate credentials of some of the impersonated organizations.
The use of legitimate RMM tools for persistent access has been a hallmark of the MuddyWater group, although the adversary has since also increasingly deployed its own malware in attacks. Both MuddyWater and Volant Manticore are assessed to be affiliated with Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS).
"While we identified multiple links to MuddyWater, we assess that Volant Manticore likely consists of former MuddyWater operators who branched off from the group and currently operate as a separate threat cluster," Check Point said in an analysis published today. "Volant Manticore's targeting priorities appear responsive to regional geopolitical developments."

Samsung is reportedly planning to increase its NAND production capacity in China, but it's unfortunately not the kind of NAND flash that will benefit regular consumers directly. According to Seoul Economic Daily, citing industry sources, Samsung plans to make roughly five times as much V9 NAND flash at its second fab in Xi'an, China, by the end of 2027. Sources tell SED that the X2 fab currently produces about 10,000 300 mm wafers of the 286-layer V9 NAND per month, and the plan is to raise that figure to around 50,000. This extra output is, to the surprise of no one, aimed at enterprise SSDs for AI data centers. It's interesting that this report has surfaced when NAND spot prices have already started falling.
As for the exact plans, the report says that Samsung will build an electroplating line in X2's empty cleanroom space, move equipment in around February 2027, and finish the conversion by November 2027. Additionally, 20% to 30% of the fab's existing V6 line will also be switched to V9. Overall, this looks like a plan to mostly shift to denser NAND inside an existing fab, rather than a brand-new factory expansion. Samsung has previously denied claims of expanding production capacity, so this might be more of a reshuffle. articles.title: Hackers Exploited CVSS 10.0 Hex.pm RCE Flaw to Compromise 6 Package Registry Servers
articles.summary:
An attacker ran operating system commands on Monday on six production servers of Hex.pm, the package registry that Elixir and Erlang developers fetch their dependencies from.
The flaw used in the attack had been in the registry's code since February 2016, and the team that maintains the service had every server on a patched build within about 15 minutes of the first malicious request.
Checks since then found no sign that any package was changed. Whether the attacker read account data such as email addresses, password hashes, and two-factor authentication secrets could not be ruled out, the team said.
What Hex Users Should Do Now
Everyone with a hex.pm account has been logged out because the maintainers replaced the keys that sign sessions and access tokens. They advise account holders to take these steps:
- Change your hex.pm password.
- Reset two-factor authentication by setting up a new authenticator entry, and store the new recovery codes.
- Log back in to the client with mix hex.user auth or, for Erlang projects, rebar3 hex user auth.
- Update the Hex client when the next release ships, expected within days, with a new registry signing system.
- Watch for phishing. Exposed email addresses may be misused, so check that links in any email about Hex go to hex.pm.
API keys do not need to be replaced, according to the team: they are random 128-bit values stored only as HMAC-SHA256 hashes, which it says cannot realistically be brute-forced. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt, whi…

Capcom Axes Live Service Game "Exoprimal" After Just 3 Years
It seems as though Sony isn't the only gaming stalwart struggling to make sense of a changing live-service gaming landscape. Exoprimal launched on Steam in July 2023 with what ought to be a convincing concept: mech suits versus dinosaurs; and it looked like Capcom had big plans for the game. However, it appears as though a compelling gameplay concept just isn't enough in a world flooded with live-service games, as the online PvP shooter failed to even crack 5,000 concurrent players on Steam. 
Now, just over three years since its launch, Capcom has announced that it will be shutting down Exoprimal for good in September 2027. Capcom has not provided a reason for the game shutting down, but it's safe to assume the low player retention is to blame. As of November 24, 2026, Exoprimal players will no longer be able to buy the Survival Pass Premium battle pass tiers. The game itself will be delisted on March 30, 2027, and the servers will shut down on September 29, 2027. There does not appear to be a post-service plan to keep the game alive at all—unlike the recently discontinued Splitgate: Arena Reloaded and Empulse, which both received a final patch allowing peer-to-peer hosting.

articles.title: The process gap holding back enterprise AI
articles.summary:
The process gap holding back enterprise AI
AI budgets keep climbing. Legacy processes are why returns stall
Current enterprise AI investment is drastically outpacing its impact. Budgets are growing and AI agents are spreading across business operations, yet many organizations have committed to AI faster than they can evaluate it and still cannot show what the spending has returned.
The gap between AI spend and results has little to do with the capability of AI models. Instead, it’s the processes AI is being asked to run that hold it back. In large organizations, from banks and insurers to manufacturers and healthcare providers, almost every process is legacy. That isn’t because they are old, but because they were designed before AI tools.
Senior Vice President of Customer Success at Camunda.
These processes were built around people handing work to one another, and each new customer requirement or regulatory shift has added more steps over time. Layered onto complex and outdated processes, AI must wait for the same sign-offs a person would, so the work moves no faster than before.
Each time an agent finishes its part of a task, the work lands back in a queue waiting for someone to pick it up. Controls built for people also struggle to govern what AI does, opening gaps the process was never designed to close. As a result, organizations end up paying for AI without getting the speed or scale it was bought for.

articles.summary:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Cuts to Chinese CSP Demand Expecting to Slow Memory Industry Revenue Growth in 2027
TrendForce's latest memory industry research indicates that Chinese Cloud Service Providers (CSPs) have reduced their 2027 memory orders, putting downward pressure on the industry's price outlook. The NAND Flash market is expected to enter a downward pricing cycle as supply continues to expand, prompting TrendForce to lower its 2027 NAND Flash revenue forecast to approximately US$419.3 billion.
Meanwhile, although the DRAM market is expected to remain undersupplied, quarterly price increases are projected to moderate. This has led TrendForce to revise its 2027 DRAM revenue forecast downward to $1.15 trillion.In the NAND Flash market, Chinese CSPs began scaling back their enterprise SSD procurement plans for 2027 in mid-4Q26 amid concerns over GPU supply shortages. These reductions have exceeded the additional orders placed by North American CSPs.
For consumer electronics products such as PCs and smartphones, low-cost memory inventories have been depleted, and device prices face upward pressure in 2027. Brands are expected to reduce NAND Flash capacity specifications across their product portfolios to keep bill-of-materials (BOM) costs under control. Together, these factors will weigh on NAND Flash bit demand growth in 2027.
